claims.statement_id: Anansi kerap digambarkan sebagai laba-laba antropomorfik berwajah manusia atau manusia bertubuh laba-laba berkaki delapan.
claims.quote: While often depicted as an animal, Anansi has many representations, which include an anthropomorphic spider with a human face, or conversely, a human with spider-like features, such as eight legs.

claims.statement: Anansi or Ananse (literally "spider") is a character in Akan religion and folklore associated with stories, wisdom, knowledge, wit, mischievousness, cunning and trickery, most commonly depicted as a spider.
claims.statement_id: Anansi atau Ananse (secara harfiah berarti laba-laba) adalah tokoh dalam agama dan cerita rakyat Akan yang terkait dengan cerita, kebijaksanaan, pengetahuan, kecerdikan, kenakalan, dan tipu daya, paling sering digambarkan sebagai laba-laba.
claims.quote: Anansi or Ananse ... literally translates to spider) is a character in Akan religion and folklore associated with stories, wisdom, knowledge, wit, mischievousness, cunning, and trickery, most commonly depicted as a spider.

claims.statement: The Akan are a close-knit people from present-day southern Ghana who rely on social order, which is conveyed through the stories of their culture.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Akan adalah masyarakat yang erat dari Ghana selatan masa kini, yang bertumpu pada tatanan sosial yang tersalur lewat cerita-cerita dari budaya mereka.
claims.quote: The Akan people are a close-knit people from present-day southern Ghana who rely on social order, which translates through the stories that come out of their culture.

claims.statement: In many ways Anansi is a paradoxical character whose actions defy this social order, but by incorporating rebellion and doubt into faith, his folkloric presence strengthens it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak hal Anansi tokoh paradoks yang tindakannya menentang tatanan sosial, tetapi dengan memasukkan pemberontakan dan keraguan ke dalam iman, kehadirannya dalam cerita rakyat justru memperkuat tatanan itu.
claims.quote: In many ways, Anansi is a paradoxical character whose actions defy this social order, but in incorporating rebellion and doubt into faith, his folkloric presence strengthens it.

claims.statement: These spider tales were spread to the Americas via the Atlantic slave trade.
claims.statement_id: Cerita-cerita laba-laba ini menyebar ke Amerika melalui perdagangan budak Atlantik.
claims.quote: These spider tales were spread to the Americas via the Atlantic slave trade.

claims.statement: Spider tales are found extensively throughout West Africa, but the Anansi tales from Ghana are seen as the origin of these stories and are among the best-known.
claims.statement_id: Cerita laba-laba ditemukan luas di Afrika Barat, tetapi kisah Anansi dari Ghana dipandang sebagai asal cerita-cerita itu dan termasuk yang paling terkenal.
claims.quote: Spider tales are found extensively throughout West Africa, but the Anansi tales from Ghana are seen to be the origin of these stories and are among the best-known

claims.statement: The tales later spread to the West Indies, Suriname, Sierra Leone (where they were introduced by Jamaican Maroons) and the Netherlands Antilles.
claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisah itu kemudian menyebar ke Hindia Barat, Suriname, Sierra Leone (dibawa oleh Maroon Jamaika), dan Antilla Belanda.
claims.quote: They later spread to the West Indies, Suriname, Sierra Leone (where they were introduced by Jamaican Maroons) and the Netherlands Antilles

claims.statement: In several folktales Anansi has a family: his long-suffering wife Okonore Yaa (known elsewhere as Aso, Crooky or Shi Maria) and his sons Ntikuma the firstborn, Tikelenkelen the big-headed, Nankonhwea with a spindly neck and legs, and Afudohwedohwe the pot-bellied.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa kisah Anansi memiliki keluarga: istrinya yang sabar, Okonore Yaa (di daerah lain dikenal sebagai Aso, Crooky, atau Shi Maria), dan putra-putranya Ntikuma si sulung, Tikelenkelen si berkepala besar, Nankonhwea yang berleher dan berkaki kurus, serta Afudohwedohwe si perut buncit.
claims.quote: Anansi also has a family in several folktales involving him, consisting of his long-suffering wife Okonore Yaa - known in other regions as Aso, Crooky, or Shi Maria; Ntikuma, his firstborn son; Tikelenkelen, his big-headed son; Nankonhwea, his son with a spindly neck and spindly legs; finally, Afudohwedohwe, his pot-bellied son.

claims.statement: Anansi stories were part of an exclusively oral tradition, and Anansi himself was seen as synonymous with skill and wisdom in speech.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Anansi merupakan bagian dari tradisi yang sepenuhnya lisan, dan Anansi sendiri dipandang identik dengan keterampilan dan kebijaksanaan berbicara.
claims.quote: Anansi stories were part of an exclusively oral tradition, and Anansi himself was seen as synonymous with skill and wisdom in speech.

claims.statement: Anansi was often celebrated as a symbol of slave resistance and survival, because he is able to turn the tables on his powerful oppressors through cunning and trickery.
claims.statement_id: Anansi sering dirayakan sebagai lambang perlawanan dan ketahanan budak, karena ia mampu membalikkan keadaan terhadap penindas yang berkuasa lewat kecerdikan dan tipu dayanya.
claims.quote: Anansi was often celebrated as a symbol of slave resistance and survival, because Anansi is able to turn the tables on his powerful oppressors by using his cunning and trickery

claims.statement: Anansi becomes both an ideal to aspire toward and a cautionary tale against the selfish desires that can cause our undoing.
claims.statement_id: Anansi menjadi sekaligus teladan yang dicita-citakan dan kisah peringatan terhadap keinginan egois yang dapat menjadi sebab kehancuran kita.
claims.quote: Anansi becomes both an ideal to be aspired toward, and a cautionary tale against the selfish desires that can cause our undoing.

claims.statement: Names for Anansi in different places include Kacou Ananzè (Côte d'Ivoire), Kwaku Ananse (Jamaica, Ghana), Bru Nansi (Virgin Islands), Anansi or Anancy (Jamaica, Grenada, Costa Rica, Colombia, Nicaragua), Anansi Drew (The Bahamas) and Aunt Nancy (South Carolina).
claims.statement_id: Nama-nama lain Anansi di berbagai daerah antara lain Kacou Ananzè (Pantai Gading), Kwaku Ananse (Jamaika, Ghana), Bru Nansi (Kepulauan Virgin), Anansi atau Anancy (Jamaika, Grenada, Kosta Rika, Kolombia, Nikaragua), Anansi Drew (Bahama), dan Aunt Nancy (Carolina Selatan).
claims.quote: Kacou Ananzè (Côte d'Ivoire) Kwaku Ananse (Jamaica), (Ghana) Bru Nansi (Virgin Islands) Anansi or Anancy (Jamaica, Grenada, Costa Rica, Colombia, Nicaragua) Anansi (Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Islands) Anansi Drew (The Bahamas) Aunt Nancy (South Carolina)

claims.statement: Anansi's name comes from the word in the Akan language for "spider".
claims.statement_id: Nama Anansi berasal dari kata dalam bahasa Akan untuk "laba-laba".
claims.quote: Anansi's name comes from the word in the Akan language for "spider".

claims.statement: One story explains how he became known as the owner of all stories in the world.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kisah menjelaskan bagaimana ia dikenal sebagai pemilik semua cerita di dunia.
claims.quote: one explains how he became known as the owner of all stories in the world.

claims.statement: In one version Anansi wanted to acquire the stories of the sky god Nyame, who held them all to himself; Nyame set him four challenges in exchange: capturing the python Onini, the hornets Mmoboro, the leopard Osebo and the dwarf Mmoatia.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi, Anansi ingin mendapatkan cerita milik dewa langit Nyame, yang menyimpan semuanya sendiri; Nyame memberinya empat tantangan sebagai imbalan: menangkap ular piton Onini, tawon Mmoboro, macan tutul Osebo, dan kurcaci Mmoatia.
claims.quote: Anansi wanted to acquire the stories of the sky god Nyame, who held all the stories to himself. Nyame tasks Anansi with four challenges in exchange for them: the capture of the python Onini, the hornets known as Mmoboro, the leopard Osebo, and the dwarf Mmoatia.

claims.statement: In the Marvel Comics series The Amazing Spider-Man volume 2 (2003), Ezekiel Sims reveals that Kwaku Anansi was the first Spider-Man.
claims.statement_id: Dalam serial Marvel Comics The Amazing Spider-Man volume 2 (2003), terungkap oleh Ezekiel Sims bahwa Kwaku Anansi adalah Spider-Man pertama.
claims.quote: In the Marvel Comics series The Amazing Spider-Man volume 2 (2003), it is revealed by Ezekiel Sims that Kwaku Anansi was the first Spider-Man.

claims.statement: Filmmaker and author Gerald McDermott created the animated short Anansi the Spider in 1969.
claims.statement_id: Pembuat film dan penulis Gerald McDermott menciptakan film animasi pendek Anansi the Spider pada 1969.
claims.quote: filmmaker and author Gerald McDermott created the animated short Anansi the Spider in 1969

claims.statement: In the olden days all the stories men told were about Nyankupon, the chief of the gods; Spider, who was very conceited, wanted the stories to be told about him.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman dahulu semua cerita yang dituturkan manusia adalah cerita tentang Nyankupon, pemimpin para dewa; Laba-laba, yang sangat sombong, ingin cerita-cerita itu dituturkan tentang dirinya.
claims.quote: In the olden days all the stories which men told were stories of Nyankupon, the chief of the gods. Spider, who was very conceited, wanted the stories to be told about him.

claims.statement: Nyankupon agreed on one condition: Spider (Anansi) must bring him three things, a jar full of live bees, a boa-constrictor and a tiger.
claims.statement_id: Nyankupon setuju dengan satu syarat: Laba-laba (Anansi) harus membawa tiga hal, yaitu sebuah guci berisi lebah hidup, seekor ular boa, dan seekor harimau.
claims.quote: Nyankupon agreed, on one condition. He told Spider (or Anansi) that he must bring him three things: the first was a jar full of live bees, the second was a boa-constrictor, and the third a tiger.

claims.statement: The bees declared that of course they could fly into the jar, and once they were safely inside Anansi sealed the jar and sent it to Nyankupon.
claims.statement_id: Lebah-lebah langsung menyatakan bahwa tentu mereka bisa terbang masuk ke guci, dan begitu mereka di dalam, Anansi menutup guci itu rapat-rapat lalu mengirimkannya kepada Nyankupon.
claims.quote: The bees immediately declared that of course they could fly into the jar-which they at once did. As soon as they were safely inside, Anansi sealed up the jar and sent it off to Nyankupon.

claims.statement: Having made the tiger helpless, he led him straight to Nyankupon's house.
claims.statement_id: Setelah membuat harimau itu tak berdaya, ia menuntunnya langsung ke rumah Nyankupon.
claims.quote: Having thus made the tiger helpless, he led him straight to Nyankupon's house.

claims.statement: Nyankupon was amazed at Spider's cleverness in fulfilling the three conditions and at once gave him permission to call all the old tales Anansi tales.
claims.statement_id: Nyankupon takjub pada kecerdikan Laba-laba memenuhi ketiga syarat itu, dan segera mengizinkannya menyebut semua dongeng lama sebagai dongeng Anansi.
claims.quote: Nyankupon was amazed at Spider's cleverness in fulfilling the three conditions. He immediately gave him permission for the future to call all the old tales Anansi tales.

claims.statement: Once there lived in Fanti-land a man named Father Anansi, who possessed all the wisdom in the world.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu di tanah Fanti hidup seorang lelaki bernama Bapa Anansi, yang memiliki semua kebijaksanaan di dunia.
claims.quote: There once lived, in Fanti-land, a man named Father Anansi. He possessed all the wisdom in the world.

claims.statement: One day the men of the country offended Father Anansi, who resolved to punish them; after much thought he decided the severest penalty would be to hide all his wisdom from them.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari para lelaki negeri itu menyinggung Bapa Anansi, yang segera bertekad menghukum mereka; setelah berpikir lama ia memutuskan hukuman terberat adalah menyembunyikan seluruh kebijaksanaannya dari mereka.
claims.quote: One day the men of the country were unfortunate enough to offend Father Anansi, who immediately resolved to punish them. After much thought he decided that the severest penalty he could inflict would be to hide all his wisdom from them.

claims.statement: Kweku Tsin watched his father's vain attempts and suggested hanging the pot on his back; in anger the father threw the pot down so that it broke, and the wisdom in it escaped and spread throughout the world.
claims.statement_id: Kweku Tsin menyaksikan upaya sia-sia ayahnya dan menyarankan agar guci digantung di punggung; dalam amarah sang ayah melempar guci itu hingga pecah, dan kebijaksanaan di dalamnya lolos serta menyebar ke seluruh dunia.
claims.quote: For some time Kweku Tsin watched his father's vain attempts. At last, unable to contain himself any longer, he cried out: "Father, why do you not hang the pot on your back? Then you could easily climb the tree." ... In his anger he threw the pot down. It struck on a great rock and broke. The wisdom contained in it escaped and spread throughout the world.

claims.statement: Anansi persuaded Nothing to change clothes for a little while, promising to give back the fine velvet before they reached the town.
claims.statement_id: Anansi membujuk Nothing bertukar pakaian sebentar dengan janji mengembalikan kain beludru yang bagus sebelum mereka tiba di kota.
claims.quote: Anansi persuaded Nothing to change clothes for a little while, promising to give back the fine velvet before they reached the town.

claims.statement: Egya Anansi is described as an exceedingly selfish and greedy man who never liked to share anything.
claims.statement_id: Egya Anansi digambarkan sebagai lelaki yang sangat egois dan serakah, yang tidak pernah suka berbagi apa pun.
claims.quote: Egya Anansi was very well pleased when he saw his wealth of corn and beans. He was, however, an exceedingly selfish and greedy man, who never liked to share anything

claims.statement: Anansi grew angry and struck the figure on the cheek with his right hand, and his hand stuck fast to the rubber.
claims.statement_id: Anansi marah dan memukul pipi sosok karet itu dengan tangan kanan, dan tangannya pun lengket pada karet.
claims.quote: Anansi then became very angry and dealt the figure a blow on the cheek with his right hand. Of course, his hand stuck fast to the rubber.

claims.statement: Anansi was so ashamed to be caught in the act of greediness that he changed into a spider and hid in a dark corner of the ceiling; since then spiders have always been found in dark, dusty corners.
claims.statement_id: Anansi begitu malu tertangkap basah serakah sehingga ia berubah menjadi laba-laba dan bersembunyi di sudut gelap langit-langit; sejak itu laba-laba selalu ditemukan di sudut gelap dan berdebu.
claims.quote: He, on the other hand, was so ashamed to be caught in the act of greediness that he changed into a spider and took refuge in a dark corner of the ceiling lest any one should see him. Since then spiders have always been found in dark, dusty corners, where people are not likely to notice them.

claims.statement: One of two influences dominating story-telling in Jamaica is the conception of the spider Anansi as the trickster hero among a group of animal figures.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu dari dua pengaruh yang mendominasi penceritaan di Jamaika adalah gagasan tentang laba-laba Anansi sebagai pahlawan penipu di antara sekelompok tokoh hewan.
claims.quote: influences have dominated story-telling in Jamaica ... the second, the conception of the spider Anansi as the trickster hero among a group of animal figures.

claims.statement: Anansi is the culture hero of the Gold Coast, a kind of god, just as Turtle is of the Slave coast and Hare (Brer Rabbit) of the Bantu people.
claims.statement_id: Anansi adalah pahlawan budaya Gold Coast, semacam dewa, seperti Kura-kura bagi Pantai Budak dan Kelinci (Brer Rabbit) bagi bangsa Bantu.
claims.quote: Anansi is the culture hero of the Gold Coast,-a kind of god-, just as Turtle is of the Slave coast and Hare (our own Brer Rabbit) of the Bantu people.

claims.statement: "Anansi stories" regularly form the entertainment during wake-nights.
claims.statement_id: Cerita Anansi secara rutin menjadi hiburan pada malam berjaga (wake-night).
claims.quote: "Anansi stories" regularly form the entertainment during wake-nights

claims.statement: The head-man on a Westmoreland cattle-pen assured the author that Anansi, once a man, was now leader of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Seorang kepala peternakan di Westmoreland meyakinkan penulis bahwa Anansi, yang dulu manusia, kini pemimpin arwah orang mati.
claims.quote: The head-man on a Westmoreland cattle-pen even assured me that Anansi, once a man, was now leader of the dead

claims.statement: Coatlicue is represented as a woman wearing a skirt of writhing snakes and a necklace made of human hearts, hands, and skulls.
claims.statement_id: Coatlicue digambarkan mengenakan rok ular dan kalung jantung serta tengkorak manusia.
claims.quote: Coatlicue is represented as a woman wearing a skirt of writhing snakes and a necklace made of human hearts, hands, and skulls.

claims.statement: Her feet and hands are adorned with claws and her breasts are depicted as hanging flaccid from pregnancy.
claims.statement_id: Kaki dan tangannya dihiasi cakar dan payudaranya digambarkan kendur karena kehamilan.
claims.quote: Her feet and hands are adorned with claws and her breasts are depicted as hanging flaccid from pregnancy.

claims.statement: According to Aztec mythology, the goddess Coatlicue became miraculously pregnant when a ball of feathers fell on her while she was sweeping a temple—an event that symbolizes divine conception and cosmic destiny.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Aztec, dewi Coatlicue hamil secara mukjizat saat menyapu kuil.
claims.quote: According to Aztec mythology, the goddess Coatlicue became miraculously pregnant when a ball of feathers fell on her while she was sweeping a temple—an event that symbolizes divine conception and cosmic destiny.

claims.statement: Coatlicue thus has creative aspects, which may balance the skulls, hearts, hands, and claws that connect her to the earth deity Tlaltecuhtli.
claims.statement_id: Coatlicue memiliki aspek penciptaan yang mengimbangi simbol maut dan keterikatannya dengan dewa bumi Tlaltecuhtli.
claims.quote: Coatlicue thus has creative aspects, which may balance the skulls, hearts, hands, and claws that connect her to the earth deity Tlaltecuhtli.

claims.statement: Coatlicue ('Serpent Skirt') was a major deity in the Aztec pantheon and regarded as the earth-mother goddess.
claims.statement_id: Coatlicue ('Rok Ular') adalah dewa penting dalam panteon Aztec dan dianggap sebagai dewi ibu bumi.
claims.quote: Coatlicue ... or 'Serpent Skirt' was a major deity in the Aztec pantheon and regarded as the earth-mother goddess.

claims.statement: Coatlicue was the patron of childbirth and was associated with warfare, governance and agriculture; she was considered the female aspect of the primordial god Ometeotl.
claims.statement_id: Coatlicue adalah pelindung persalinan dan dikaitkan dengan perang, pemerintahan, dan pertanian. Ia dianggap sebagai aspek perempuan dari dewa purba Ometeotl.
claims.quote: Coatlicue was the patron of childbirth and was associated with warfare, governance and agriculture. She was considered the female aspect of the primordial god Ometeotl.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology Coatlicue was a priestess who maintained the shrine on top of the sacred mountain Coatepec; while she was sweeping, a ball of feathers descended from the heavens and, when she tucked it into her belt, miraculously impregnated her.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Coatlicue adalah seorang pendeta perempuan yang bertugas merawat kuil di puncak gunung suci Coatepec. Suatu hari, saat ia menyapu, sebuah bola bulu turun dari langit; ketika ia menyelipkannya di ikat pinggang, ia hamil secara ajaib.
claims.quote: In Aztec mythology, Coatlicue was actually a priestess whose job was to maintain the shrine on the top of the legendary sacred mountain Coatepec ... One day, as she was sweeping, a ball of feathers descended from the heavens and when she tucked it into her belt it miraculously impregnated her.

claims.statement: The resulting child was the powerful Aztec god of war Huitzilopochtli.
claims.statement_id: Anak yang lahir dari kehamilan itu adalah Huitzilopochtli, dewa perang Aztec yang perkasa.
claims.quote: The resulting child was none other than the powerful Aztec god of war Huitzilopochtli.

claims.statement: Rising to his mother's defence, the god sprang from the womb fully grown and fully armed as an invincible warrior.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membela ibunya, sang dewa melompat keluar dari rahim dalam keadaan dewasa penuh dan bersenjata lengkap sebagai prajurit yang tak terkalahkan.
claims.quote: Rising to his mother's defence the god sprang from the womb fully grown and fully armed as an invincible warrior.

claims.statement: In another myth Coatlicue warned the Mexica of their future demise: the Aztec cities would fall one by one, and only then would her son Huitzilopochtli return to her side.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah mitos lain, Coatlicue memperingatkan bangsa Mexica tentang kehancuran mereka di masa depan: kota-kota Aztec akan jatuh satu per satu, dan baru setelah itu putranya, Huitzilopochtli, akan kembali ke sisinya.
claims.quote: Coatlicue warned the Mexica of their future demise ... the goddess revealed that the Aztec cities would fall one by one. Then, and only then, would her son Huitzilopochtli return to her side.

claims.statement: The goddess was worshipped in the spring ritual of Tozozontli in the rainy season and in the autumnal hunting festival of Quecholli, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewi dipuja dalam ritual musim semi Tozozontli pada musim hujan dan dalam perayaan berburu musim gugur Quecholli, ketika seorang peniru sang dewi dikorbankan.
claims.quote: The goddess was worshipped in the spring ritual of Tozozontli in the rainy season and in the autumnal hunting festival of Quecholli, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed.

claims.statement: In art, Coatlicue is most famously represented in the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan, which now resides in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni, Coatlicue paling terkenal digambarkan oleh patung basal raksasa yang ditemukan di Tenochtitlan dan kini berada di Museum Nasional Antropologi di Mexico City.
claims.quote: In art, Coatlicue is most famously represented in the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan which now resides in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City.

claims.statement: In that depiction she wears her typical skirt of entwined snakes, and her hands and feet have large claws which she uses to rip up human corpses before she eats them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambaran itu, ia mengenakan rok khasnya dari ular yang terjalin, sementara tangan dan kakinya bercakar besar yang ia pakai untuk mencabik mayat manusia sebelum memakannya.
claims.quote: She also wears her typical skirt of entwined snakes whilst her hands and feet have the large claws which she uses to rip up human corpses before she eats them.

claims.statement: Interpreting this as dishonor, her daughter Coyolxauhqui, along with her 400 brothers, plotted to kill her; as the attack began, Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed from his mother, defeated his siblings, and cast Coyolxauhqui into the sky, where she became the moon.
claims.statement_id: Menganggap kehamilan itu sebagai aib, putrinya Coyolxauhqui bersama 400 saudara laki-lakinya merencanakan pembunuhan terhadap ibu mereka. Saat serangan dimulai, Huitzilopochtli keluar dengan senjata lengkap dari tubuh ibunya, mengalahkan saudara-saudaranya, dan melempar Coyolxauhqui ke langit, tempat ia menjadi bulan.
claims.quote: Interpreting this as dishonor, her daughter Coyolxauhqui, along with her 400 brothers, plotted to kill her. Just as the attack began, Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed from his mother, defeated his siblings, and cast Coyolxauhqui into the sky, where she became the moon.

issues.message: Tidak muncul di kutipan mana pun: Serikat. Tambahkan klaim yang kutipannya memuat hal ini, atau hapus dari teks.

claims.statement: Whoever hears her crying is said to either suffer misfortune, death, or become extremely unsuccessful in life.
claims.statement_id: Siapa pun yang mendengar tangisannya konon akan tertimpa kemalangan atau kematian.
claims.quote: Whoever hears her crying is said to either suffer misfortune, death, or become extremely unsuccessful in life.

claims.statement: The lore of La Llorona is well known in Mexico and the southwestern United States.
claims.statement_id: Cerita La Llorona sangat dikenal di Mexico dan barat daya United States.
claims.quote: The lore of La Llorona is well known in Mexico and the southwestern United States.

claims.statement: The presence of ghostly beings who cry by rivers for various reasons is a recurring feature of the mythology of Mesoamerican peoples.
claims.statement_id: Keberadaan hantu yang menangis di dekat sungai merupakan ciri berulang dalam mitologi Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: The presence of ghostly beings who cry by rivers for various reasons is a recurring feature of the mythology of Mesoamerican peoples.

claims.statement: The legend of La Llorona is, above all, a story created to warn and frighten.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini merupakan cerita yang dibuat untuk memberi peringatan dan menakuti orang.
claims.quote: The legend of La Llorona is, above all, a story created to warn and frighten.

claims.statement: La Llorona ('the Crying Woman, the Weeping Woman, the Wailer') is a vengeful ghost in Hispanic American folklore who is said to roam near bodies of water mourning her children she drowned in the river.
claims.statement_id: La Llorona ('Perempuan yang Menangis', 'Pemeratap') adalah hantu pendendam dalam cerita rakyat Hispanik Amerika yang dikatakan berkeliaran di dekat perairan sambil meratapi anak-anaknya yang ia tenggelamkan di sungai.
claims.quote: 'the Crying Woman, the Weeping Woman, the Wailer') is a vengeful ghost in Hispanic American folklore who is said to roam near bodies of water mourning her children she drowned in the river.

claims.statement: 'La Llorona' literally means 'the weeping woman', so it is not surprising that the main characteristic shared by all stories of La Llorona is that she weeps.
claims.statement_id: 'La Llorona' secara harfiah berarti 'perempuan yang menangis'; ciri utama yang sama pada semua kisah La Llorona adalah bahwa ia menangis.
claims.quote: “La Llorona” literally means “the weeping woman,” so it’s not surprising that the main characteristic shared by all stories of “La Llorona” is that she weeps.

claims.statement: In Latin America, in Spanish-speaking communities in the U.S., and especially in Mexico, no ghost story is told, discussed, or interpreted as often or as widely as the legend of La Llorona.
claims.statement_id: Di Amerika Latin, di komunitas berbahasa Spanyol di AS, dan terutama di Mexico, tidak ada kisah hantu yang diceritakan, dibahas, dan ditafsirkan sesering dan seluas legenda La Llorona.
claims.quote: In Latin America, in Spanish-speaking communities in the U.S., and especially in Mexico, no ghost story is told as often, discussed as enthusiastically, or interpreted as widely, as the legend of La Llorona.

claims.statement: La Llorona is often closely associated with children. In some stories she wails for her own lost or dead children; in many of these she killed her own children when she was alive and is doomed for her actions to be a wandering ghost.
claims.statement_id: La Llorona sering dikaitkan erat dengan anak-anak. Dalam sebagian kisah ia meratapi anaknya yang hilang atau mati; dalam banyak di antaranya ia membunuh anaknya sendiri semasa hidup dan, karena perbuatan itu, ditakdirkan menjadi hantu pengembara.
claims.quote: La Llorona is often closely associated with children. In some stories, she is said to wail for her own lost or dead children; in many of these stories, she killed her own children when she was alive and is doomed for her actions to be a wandering ghost.

claims.statement: In other stories La Llorona appears mainly to women who have children, and in still others she kidnaps children, who are never seen again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah lain La Llorona terutama menampakkan diri kepada perempuan yang punya anak, dan dalam kisah lainnya lagi ia menculik anak-anak yang tidak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: La Llorona is often closely associated with children. ... In other stories, she appears mainly to women who have children, while in still others, she kidnaps children, who are never seen again.

claims.statement: La Llorona typically appears as a malevolent spirit, either a harbinger or a direct cause of misfortune to the living; sometimes she takes the form of a 'dangerous siren' tempting a solitary man late at night as a pitiful figure hidden under a rebozo.
claims.statement_id: La Llorona biasanya muncul sebagai roh jahat, baik sebagai pertanda maupun penyebab langsung kemalangan bagi yang hidup. Kadang ia berwujud 'sirene berbahaya' yang menggoda seorang pria yang sendirian larut malam sebagai sosok malang yang tersembunyi di balik rebozo.
claims.quote: La Llorona typically appears as a malevolent spirit, either a harbinger or a direct cause of misfortune to the living. Sometimes she takes the form of a “dangerous siren,” tempting a solitary male late at night by confronting him as a pitiful, woebegone figure hidden under a rebozo.

claims.statement: Most typically La Llorona is heard weeping and shrieking through the night, and a chance meeting with her is dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Yang paling lazim, La Llorona terdengar menangis dan menjerit sepanjang malam, dan berjumpa dengannya secara kebetulan berbahaya.
claims.quote: La Llorona typically appears as a malevolent spirit, either a harbinger or a direct cause of misfortune to the living. ... most typically, she is heard weeping and shrieking through the night. A chance meeting with her is dangerous.

claims.statement: Stories vary: sometimes La Llorona sees you from afar and pursues you; sometimes she appears in your horse-drawn wagon or car, warning you against bad behavior, before disappearing. In some stories an encounter with her is fatal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam berbagai kisah, kadang La Llorona melihat orang dari kejauhan lalu mengejarnya; kadang ia muncul di kereta kuda atau mobil, memperingatkan agar tidak berperilaku buruk, lalu menghilang. Dalam sebagian kisah, perjumpaan dengannya berakibat fatal.
claims.quote: Looking through such stories, you’ll find many variations: sometimes La Llorona sees you from afar and pursues you, terrifying you as you flee toward your home. ... Sometimes she appears in your horse-drawn wagon or in your car, warning you against bad behavior, before disappearing ... In some stories, an encounter with her is fatal.

claims.statement: In one account the people heard a weeping woman night after night; she passed by in the middle of the night, wailing and crying out in a loud voice: 'My children, we must flee far away from this city!' and at other times: 'My children, where shall I take you?'
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah catatan, orang-orang mendengar seorang perempuan menangis malam demi malam; ia lewat di tengah malam sambil meratap dengan suara keras: 'Anak-anakku, kita harus lari jauh dari kota ini!' dan pada saat lain: 'Anak-anakku, ke mana akan kubawa kalian?'
claims.quote: The people heard a weeping woman night after night. She passed by in the middle of the night, wailing and crying out in a loud voice: “My children, we must flee far away from this city!” At other times she cried: “My children, where shall I take you?”

claims.statement: The weeping-woman story is actually a Nahuatl account of a bad omen that occurred in Tenochtitlan (now Mexico City) in 1509, ten years before the arrival of Hernán Cortés and his Spanish troops, with details like a traditional La Llorona encounter story.
claims.statement_id: Kisah perempuan menangis itu ternyata catatan berbahasa Nahuatl tentang pertanda buruk yang terjadi di Tenochtitlan (kini Mexico City) pada 1509, sepuluh tahun sebelum Hernán Cortés dan pasukan Spanyolnya tiba, dan rinciannya sesuai dengan kisah perjumpaan La Llorona yang tradisional.
claims.quote: This certainly falls within the range of details we would expect in a traditional La Llorona encounter story. But it’s actually a Náhuatl account of a bad omen that occurred in Tenochtitlan (now Mexico city) in 1509, ten years before the arrival of Hernán Cortés and his Spanish troops.

claims.statement: These similarities between La Llorona and Cihuacoatl have led many scholars to believe that the traditional image of La Llorona (and the stories about her that are mostly descriptions) derives from this Aztec belief.
claims.statement_id: Kemiripan antara La Llorona dan Cihuacoatl membuat banyak ahli percaya bahwa citra tradisional La Llorona (dan kisah-kisah tentangnya yang kebanyakan berupa deskripsi) berasal dari kepercayaan Aztec ini.
claims.quote: These similarities between La Llorona and Cihuacoatl have led many scholars to believe that the traditional image of La Llorona (and thus the stories about her that are mostly descriptions) derive from this Aztec belief.

claims.statement: A scholar quoted in the source holds that the literary legend of La Llorona struck deep roots in Mexican tradition because it was grafted on an Indian legend cycle about the supernatural woman who seduces men out alone on the roads or working in the fields.
claims.statement_id: Seorang folklorwan yang dikutip dalam sumber ini berpendapat bahwa legenda sastra La Llorona berakar kuat dalam tradisi Mexico karena dicangkokkan pada siklus legenda Indian tentang perempuan gaib yang menggoda pria yang sendirian di jalan atau sedang bekerja di ladang.
claims.quote: The literary legend of La Llorona struck deep roots in Mexican tradition because it was grafted on an Indian legend cycle about the supernatural woman who seduces men when they are out alone on the roads or working in the fields.

claims.statement: A scholar quoted in the source states that the events of the 'La Llorona' story take place in an Europeanized milieu, and the characters' values and responses are thoroughly Spanish, not Indian.
claims.statement_id: Seorang ahli yang dikutip dalam sumber ini menyatakan bahwa peristiwa dalam kisah 'La Llorona' terjadi dalam lingkungan yang telah dieropakan, dan nilai serta tanggapan para tokohnya sepenuhnya Spanyol, bukan Indian.
claims.quote: The events of the “La Llorona” story take place in an Europeanized milieu, and the characters’ values, their responses, are thoroughly Spanish, not Indian.

claims.statement: According to the source's author, the current complex of La Llorona stories has deep roots among indigenous peoples throughout what is now Latin America; at some point after 1529 and before 1859, new elements arrived from Spain, and possibly other parts of Europe such as Germany.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis sumber ini, kumpulan kisah La Llorona yang sekarang berakar dalam pada masyarakat adat di seluruh wilayah yang kini disebut Amerika Latin; pada suatu waktu setelah 1529 dan sebelum 1859, unsur-unsur baru kisah itu datang dari Spanyol dan mungkin dari bagian Eropa lain seperti Jerman.
claims.quote: The current complex of stories about La Llorona has deep roots among indigenous peoples throughout what is now Latin America. At some point after 1529 and before 1859, new elements of the story arrived from Spain, and possibly other parts of Europe such as Germany.

claims.statement: The author of the source found a story about La Llorona published in Spain in 1866 by José Maria León y Domínguez, a Jesuit academic from Cadiz.
claims.statement_id: Penulis sumber ini menemukan sebuah kisah tentang La Llorona yang diterbitkan di Spanyol pada 1866 oleh José Maria León y Domínguez, seorang akademisi Jesuit dari Cadiz.
claims.quote: It’s a story I haven’t seen mentioned before in the literature on La Llorona. It was published in Spain in 1866 by José Maria León y Domínguez, a Jesuit academic from Cadiz.

claims.statement: One outgrowth of this merging of Native and Spanish elements is a strong contemporary tradition that equates La Llorona with La Malinche, the Native woman whose language skills were instrumental in Hernán Cortés's conquest of Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu hasil perpaduan unsur Pribumi dan Spanyol ini adalah tradisi kuat masa kini yang menyamakan La Llorona dengan La Malinche, perempuan Pribumi yang kemampuan bahasanya berperan penting dalam penaklukan Mexico oleh Hernán Cortés.
claims.quote: One interesting outgrowth of this merging of Native and Spanish elements is a strong contemporary tradition equates La Llorona with La Malinche, the Native woman whose language skills were instrumental in Hernán Cortés’s conquest of Mexico.

claims.statement: According to the source's author, the earliest account of the ghost's human origins that he could find comes from a poem entitled 'La Llorona' by Manuel Carpio, published in 1849.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis sumber ini, catatan tertua tentang asal-usul manusiawi hantu itu yang ia temukan berasal dari puisi berjudul 'La Llorona' karya Manuel Carpio yang terbit pada 1849.
claims.quote: accounts of the ghost’s human origins. He characterizes them as “literary” because many of the earliest of them arise in literary sources. The earliest such account that I could find comes from a poem by Manuel Carpio published in 1849 and entitled “La Llorona”

claims.statement: The word 'llorona' exists in formal Spanish separately from this legend, especially in reference to professional mourners or plañideras; in more common colloquial speech it is often used to mean 'crybaby'.
claims.statement_id: Kata 'llorona' ada dalam bahasa Spanyol baku terlepas dari legenda ini, terutama untuk menyebut peratap bayaran atau plañideras; dalam percakapan sehari-hari kata itu sering berarti 'cengeng'.
claims.quote: The word “llorona” exists in formal Spanish separately from this legend, especially in reference to professional mourners or plañideras. In more common and colloquial speech, it is often used to mean “crybaby.”

claims.statement: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird adalah roh serupa burung mitologis dalam sejarah dan kebudayaan masyarakat pribumi Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture.

claims.statement: The thunderbird is considered a supernatural being of power and strength.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird dianggap sebagai makhluk gaib yang berkuasa dan kuat.
claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture. It is considered a supernatural being of power and strength.

claims.statement: In Algonquian mythology, the thunderbird controls the upper world while the underworld is governed by the underwater panther or Great Horned Serpent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Algonquian, thunderbird menguasai alam atas sementara dunia bawah diperintah makhluk lain.
claims.quote: In Algonquian mythology, the thunderbird controls the upper world while the underworld is governed by the underwater panther or Great Horned Serpent.

claims.statement: Across cultures, thunderbirds are generally depicted as birds of prey, or hybrids of humans and birds.
claims.statement_id: Di berbagai kebudayaan makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa atau perpaduan manusia dan burung.
claims.quote: Across cultures, thunderbirds are generally depicted as birds of prey, or hybrids of humans and birds.

claims.statement: The thunderbird is said to create thunder by flapping its wings in Algonquian tellings, and lightning by flashing its eyes in both Algonquian and Iroquois tellings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Algonquian, thunderbird dikatakan menciptakan guntur dengan mengepakkan sayap; dalam penuturan Algonquian dan Iroquois, ia menciptakan petir dengan mengerjapkan matanya.
claims.quote: The thunderbird is said to create thunder by flapping its wings in Algonquian tellings, and lightning by flashing its eyes in both Algonquian and Iroquois tellings.

claims.statement: Thunderbirds are often viewed as protectors, sometimes intervening on people's behalf, but expecting veneration, prayers, and gifts.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird sering dipandang sebagai pelindung yang kadang turun tangan membela manusia, tetapi mengharapkan penghormatan, doa, dan persembahan.
claims.quote: Thunderbirds are often viewed as protectors, sometimes intervening on people's behalf, but expecting veneration, prayers, and gifts.

claims.statement: The Ojibwe version of the myth states that the thunderbirds were created by Nanabozho to fight the underwater spirits; thunderbirds also punished humans who broke moral rules.
claims.statement_id: Versi Ojibwe menyatakan bahwa thunderbird diciptakan oleh Nanabozho untuk melawan roh-roh bawah air. Thunderbird juga menghukum manusia yang melanggar aturan moral.
claims.quote: The Ojibwe version of the myth states that the thunderbirds were created by Nanabozho to fight the underwater spirits. Thunderbirds also punished humans who broke moral rules.

claims.statement: In Menominee (Northern Wisconsin) folklore, thunderbirds live on a far-western mountain that floats, control the rain and hail, delight in fighting, and continually fight the great horned snakes (the Misikinubik) to keep them from overrunning the earth and devouring humankind.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Menominee (Wisconsin utara), thunderbird tinggal di gunung terapung di sebelah barat jauh, mengendalikan hujan dan hujan es, gemar bertarung, dan terus melawan ular bertanduk besar (Misikinubik) agar tidak menguasai bumi dan melahap umat manusia.
claims.quote: In Menominee (Northern Wisconsin) folklore, thunderbirds live on a far-western mountain that floats. The thunderbirds control the rain and hail, and delight in fighting. They continually fight the great horned snakes (the Misikinubik) to keep them from overrunning the earth and devouring humankind.

claims.statement: Ho-Chunk tradition states that a man who has a vision of a thunderbird during a solitary fast will become a war chief of the people.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Ho-Chunk menyatakan bahwa seorang pria yang mendapat penglihatan tentang thunderbird saat berpuasa menyendiri akan menjadi kepala perang bagi rakyatnya.
claims.quote: Ho-Chunk tradition states that a man who has a vision of a thunderbird during a solitary fast will become a war chief of the people.

claims.statement: The thunderbird creates not just thunder (with its wing-flapping) but also lightning bolts, which it casts at the underworld creatures.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird menciptakan bukan hanya guntur (dengan kepakan sayap) tetapi juga sambaran petir yang ia lemparkan kepada makhluk-makhluk dunia bawah.
claims.quote: The thunderbird creates not just thunder (with its wing-flapping) but also lightning bolts, which it casts at the underworld creatures.

claims.statement: Petroglyphs of thunderbirds are found near Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin, in a shelter that was probably used c. 250 BCE to 1500 CE.
claims.statement_id: Petroglif thunderbird ditemukan dekat Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin, di sebuah ceruk yang kemungkinan digunakan sekitar 250 SM sampai 1500 M.
claims.quote: Petroglyphs of thunderbirds are found near Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin. They are in a shelter that was probably used c. 250 BCE to 1500 CE.

claims.statement: Stories about the struggle between the Thunderbird and Whale have been traditionally told by various Pacific coast tribal groups.
claims.statement_id: Kisah tentang pergulatan antara Thunderbird dan Paus secara tradisional diceritakan oleh berbagai kelompok suku di pesisir Pasifik.
claims.quote: Stories about the struggle between the Thunderbird and Whale (q.v.) have been traditionally told by various Pacific coast tribal groups.

claims.statement: The thunderbird is frequently depicted in the art, songs, and oral histories of many Pacific Northwest Coast cultures, but is also found in various forms among some peoples of the American Southwest, US East Coast, Great Lakes, and Great Plains.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird sering digambarkan dalam seni, lagu, dan sejarah lisan banyak budaya Pesisir Barat Laut Pasifik, tetapi juga ditemukan dalam berbagai bentuk di antara sebagian masyarakat di Barat Daya Amerika, Pesisir Timur AS, Danau-Danau Besar, dan Dataran Besar.
claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture. ... It is frequently depicted in the art, songs, and oral histories of many Pacific Northwest Coast cultures, but is also found in various forms among some peoples of the American Southwest, US East Coast, Great Lakes, and Great Plains.

claims.statement: Although Indigenous traditions hold that the Thunderbird is not a physical entity but a spirit, its name is also lent to a loose subset of allegedly undiscovered animals reported over North America.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun tradisi Pribumi memandang Thunderbird sebagai roh dan bukan makhluk fisik, namanya juga dipinjam untuk sekelompok hewan yang diduga belum ditemukan dan dilaporkan di seluruh Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: Although Indigenous traditions hold that the Thunderbird is not a physical entity but a spirit, the Thunderbird also lends its namesake to a loose subset of allegedly undiscovered animals reported over North America.

claims.statement: Thunderbird is a supernatural creature prominent in many Indigenous traditional stories and plays varying roles in different Indigenous traditions.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird adalah makhluk gaib yang menonjol dalam banyak kisah tradisional masyarakat Pribumi dan berperan berbeda-beda dalam tiap tradisi.
claims.quote: Thunderbird is a supernatural creature prominent in many Indigenous traditional stories. The thunderbird plays varying roles in different Indigenous traditions.

claims.statement: In some Indigenous traditional stories, thunder and lightning are attributed to the thunderbird, which produces thunder by flapping its wings and lightning by opening and closing its eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian kisah tradisional Pribumi, guntur dan petir dikaitkan dengan thunderbird; ia menghasilkan guntur dengan mengepakkan sayap dan petir dengan membuka dan menutup mata.
claims.quote: In some Indigenous traditional stories, thunder and lightning are attributed to the thunderbird. It produces thunder by flapping its wings and lightning by opening and closing its eyes.

claims.statement: In other traditions the thunderbird is said to hunt whales, using its wings to shoot arrows; among some Plains First Nations, thunderstorms are a contest between the thunderbird and a huge rattlesnake.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi lain, thunderbird dikatakan memburu paus dengan sayap yang melepaskan anak panah. Di antara sebagian Bangsa Pertama Dataran, badai petir adalah pertarungan antara thunderbird dan seekor ular derik raksasa.
claims.quote: In other traditions, the thunderbird is said to hunt whales, using its wings to shoot arrows. Among some Plains First Nations, thunderstorms are a contest between the thunderbird and a huge rattlesnake.

claims.statement: Individuals who had been struck by lightning and survived often became shamans, for they had received the power of the bird.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang pernah tersambar petir dan selamat sering menjadi syaman, karena mereka dianggap telah menerima kekuatan burung itu.
claims.quote: Individuals who had been struck by lightning and survived often became Shamans, for they had received the power of the bird

claims.statement: Thunderbird is described as an enormous bird (according to many Northwestern tribes, large enough to carry a killer whale in its talons as an eagle carries a fish) responsible for the sound of thunder (and in some cases lightning as well).
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird digambarkan sebagai burung raksasa (menurut banyak suku di barat laut, cukup besar untuk membawa paus pembunuh dalam cakarnya seperti elang membawa ikan) yang bertanggung jawab atas bunyi guntur (dan dalam beberapa kasus petir juga).
claims.quote: Thunderbird is described as an enormous bird (according to many Northwestern tribes, large enough to carry a killer whale in its talons as an eagle carries a fish) who is responsible for the sound of thunder (and in some cases lightning as well.)

claims.statement: In some tribes thunderbirds are considered extremely sacred forces of nature, while in others they are treated as powerful but otherwise ordinary members of the animal kingdom; in Gros Ventre tradition it was Thunderbird (Bha'a) who gave the sacred pipe to the people.
claims.statement_id: Di sebagian suku, thunderbird dianggap kekuatan alam yang sangat suci, sedangkan di suku lain diperlakukan sebagai anggota dunia hewan yang kuat namun biasa; dalam tradisi Gros Ventre, Thunderbird (Bha'a) yang memberikan pipa suci kepada rakyat.
claims.quote: In some tribes, Thunderbirds are considered extremely sacred forces of nature, while in others, they are treated like powerful but otherwise ordinary members of the animal kingdom. In Gros Ventre tradition, it was Thunderbird (Bha'a) who gave the sacred pipe to the people.

claims.statement: Thunderbirds are also used as clan animals in some Native American cultures; tribes with Thunderbird Clans include the Kwakiutl and Ho-Chunk, and on the Northwest Coast the thunderbird symbol is often used as a totem pole crest.
claims.statement_id: Thunderbird juga dipakai sebagai hewan klan di sebagian budaya Pribumi Amerika; suku dengan Klan Thunderbird mencakup Kwakiutl dan Ho-Chunk, dan di Pesisir Barat Laut simbol thunderbird sering dipakai sebagai lambang di tiang totem.
claims.quote: Thunderbirds are also used as clan animals in some Native American cultures. Tribes with Thunderbird Clans include the Kwakiutl and Ho-Chunk tribes. On the Northwest Coast, the thunderbird symbol is often used as a totem pole crest.

claims.statement: It is closely related to the deity Qʼuqʼumatz of the Kʼicheʼ people and to Quetzalcoatl of Aztec mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kukulkan memiliki kaitan erat dengan Qʼuqʼumatz bangsa Kʼicheʼ dan Quetzalcoatl dalam mitologi Aztec.
claims.quote: It is closely related to the deity Qʼuqʼumatz of the Kʼicheʼ people and to Quetzalcoatl of Aztec mythology.

claims.statement: Prominent temples to Kukulkan are found at archaeological sites in the Yucatán Peninsula, such as Chichen Itza, Uxmal and Mayapan.
claims.statement_id: Kuil untuk Kukulkan ditemukan di situs arkeologi Chichen Itza, Uxmal, dan Mayapan.
claims.quote: Prominent temples to Kukulkan are found at archaeological sites in the Yucatán Peninsula, such as Chichen Itza, Uxmal and Mayapan.

claims.statement: The depiction of the Feathered Serpent is present in other cultures of Mesoamerica.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran Ular Bersayap ada dalam kebudayaan lain di Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: The depiction of the Feathered Serpent is present in other cultures of Mesoamerica.

claims.statement: Although heavily Mexicanised, Kukulkan has its origins among the Maya of the Classic Period.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun sangat dipengaruhi budaya Meksiko, Kukulkan berakar dari bangsa Maya Periode Klasik.
claims.quote: Although heavily Mexicanised, Kukulkan has its origins among the Maya of the Classic Period.

claims.statement: The Yucatec form of the name is formed from the word kuk 'feather' with the adjectival suffix -ul, giving kukul 'feathered', combined with kan 'snake', giving a literal meaning of 'feathered snake'.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk Yucatec dari nama itu dibentuk dari kata kuk 'bulu' dengan akhiran sifat -ul sehingga menjadi kukul 'berbulu', digabung dengan kan 'ular', yang berarti harfiah 'ular berbulu'.
claims.quote: The Yucatec form of the name is formed from the word kuk "feather" with the adjectival suffix -ul, giving kukul "feathered", combined with kan "snake" (Tzotzil chon), giving a literal meaning of "feathered snake".

claims.statement: Kukulkan has its origins among the Maya of the Classic Period, when it was known as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, the War Serpent.
claims.statement_id: Kukulkan berakar pada bangsa Maya Periode Klasik, ketika ia dikenal sebagai Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, Ular Perang.
claims.quote: Kukulkan has its origins among the Maya of the Classic Period, when it was known as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan ... the War Serpent.

claims.statement: The cult of Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl was the first Mesoamerican religion to transcend the old Classic Period linguistic and ethnic divisions and facilitated communication and peaceful trade among peoples of many different social and ethnic backgrounds.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl adalah agama Mesoamerika pertama yang melampaui sekat bahasa dan etnis Periode Klasik, dan memudahkan komunikasi serta perdagangan damai antara masyarakat dari beragam latar sosial dan etnis.
claims.quote: The cult of Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl was the first Mesoamerican religion to transcend the old Classic Period linguistic and ethnic divisions. This cult facilitated communication and peaceful trade among peoples of many different social and ethnic backgrounds.

claims.statement: The cult was originally centred on the ancient city of Chichen Itza in the modern Mexican state of Yucatán and spread as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan itu semula berpusat di kota kuno Chichen Itza di negara bagian Yucatán, Meksiko modern, lalu menyebar sampai Dataran Tinggi Guatemala dan Belize utara.
claims.quote: The cult of Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl ... Although the cult was originally centred on the ancient city of Chichen Itza in the modern Mexican state of Yucatán, it spread as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.

claims.statement: In Yucatán, references to the deity Kukulkan are confused with references to a historical individual who bore the god's name, who appears to have been a ruler or priest at Chichen Itza who first appeared around the 10th century.
claims.statement_id: Di Yucatán, rujukan pada dewa Kukulkan bercampur dengan rujukan pada seorang tokoh historis yang memakai nama sang dewa; tokoh ini tampaknya penguasa atau pendeta di Chichen Itza yang pertama muncul sekitar abad ke-10.
claims.quote: In Yucatán, references to the deity Kukulkan are confused by references to a historical individual who bore the name of the god. ... This individual appears to have been a ruler or priest at Chichen Itza who first appeared around the 10th century.

claims.statement: El Castillo at Chichen Itza served as a temple to Kukulkan. At the spring and fall equinoxes the shadow cast by the sun on the edges of the nine steps of the pyramid, combined with the northern stairway and the stone serpent head carvings, creates the illusion of a massive serpent descending the pyramid.
claims.statement_id: El Castillo di Chichen Itza berfungsi sebagai kuil Kukulkan. Pada ekuinoks musim semi dan gugur, bayangan dari sudut matahari dan tepi sembilan undakan piramida, dipadukan dengan tangga utara dan ukiran kepala ular batu, menciptakan ilusi ular raksasa yang menuruni piramida.
claims.quote: El Castillo, Chichen Itza served as a temple to Kukulkan. During the spring and fall equinoxes the shadow cast by the angle of the sun and edges of the nine steps of the pyramid combined with the northern stairway and the stone serpent head carvings create the illusion of a massive serpent descending the pyramid.

claims.statement: A modern collection of folklore from Yucatán tells how Kukulkan was a winged serpent that flew to the sun and tried to speak to it, but the sun, in its pride, burnt his tongue; the same source says Kukulkan always travels ahead of the Yucatec Maya rain god Chaac, helping to predict the rains as his tail moves the winds and sweeps the earth clean.
claims.statement_id: Kumpulan cerita rakyat modern dari Yucatán menuturkan Kukulkan sebagai ular bersayap yang terbang ke matahari dan mencoba berbicara dengannya, tetapi matahari yang congkak membakar lidahnya. Sumber yang sama menyebut Kukulkan selalu berjalan di depan dewa hujan Maya Yucatec, Chaac, membantu meramalkan hujan karena ekornya menggerakkan angin dan menyapu bumi hingga bersih.
claims.quote: A modern collection of folklore from Yucatán tells how Kukulkan was a winged serpent that flew to the sun and tried to speak to it but the sun, in its pride, burnt his tongue. The same source relates how Kukulkan always travels ahead of the Yucatec Maya rain god Chaac, helping to predict the rains as his tail moves the winds and sweeps the earth clean.

claims.statement: Among the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas, Kukulkan is an evil, monstrous snake that is the pet of the sun god.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Maya Lacandon di Chiapas, Kukulkan adalah ular jahat dan menyeramkan yang menjadi peliharaan dewa matahari.
claims.quote: Among the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas, Kukulkan is an evil, monstrous snake that is the pet of the sun god.

claims.statement: In one tale, Kukulkan is a boy who was born as a snake; as he grew older it became obvious that he was the plumed serpent, and his sister cared for him in a cave.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, Kukulkan adalah anak lelaki yang lahir sebagai ular; seiring ia tumbuh, jelas bahwa ia adalah ular berbulu, dan saudara perempuannya merawatnya di sebuah gua.
claims.quote: In one tale, Kukulkan is a boy who was born as a snake. As he grew older it became obvious that he was the plumed serpent and his sister cared for him in a cave.

claims.statement: In the 2006 film Apocalypto, the high priest in charge of human sacrifice prays to Kukulkan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film Apocalypto (2006), imam agung yang bertanggung jawab atas pengorbanan manusia berdoa kepada Kukulkan.
claims.quote: In the 2006 film Apocalypto, the high priest in charge of human sacrifice prays to Kukulkan.

claims.statement: In the 2002 video game Serious Sam: The Second Encounter, Kukulkan serves as a guardian of the time portal in Teotihuacan and is fought as that game's first boss.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gim video Serious Sam: The Second Encounter (2002), Kukulkan menjadi penjaga portal waktu di Teotihuacan dan dilawan sebagai bos pertama gim itu.
claims.quote: In the 2002 video game Serious Sam: The Second Encounter, Kukulkan serves as a guardian of the time portal in Teotihuacan and is fought as that game's first boss.

claims.statement: Kukulcan is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular the Yucatec Maya; he is also identified as Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and as Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.
claims.statement_id: Kukulcan adalah nama dewa ular berbulu dalam mitologi dan agama Mesoamerika, khususnya Maya Yucatec. Ia juga diidentifikasi sebagai dewa ular berbulu Quetzalcóatl oleh bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, sebagai Gucumatz oleh Maya Quiché di Guatemala, dan sebagai Ehecatl, dewa angin bangsa Huastec di Pesisir Teluk.
claims.quote: Kukulcan (pron. Koo-kool-kan) is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular, the Yucatec Maya. He is also identified as the feathered serpent god Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.

claims.statement: The chief god of the Yucatec Maya, who settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica, was the feathered serpent Kukulcan, whose name means feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan); he was a creator god and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.
claims.statement_id: Dewa utama Maya Yucatec, yang menetap di semenanjung Yucatan di utara Mesoamerika kuno, adalah ular berbulu Kukulcan, yang namanya berarti 'berbulu' (k'uk'ul) dan 'ular' (kan). Ia adalah dewa pencipta serta dewa hujan, angin, badai, dan kehidupan.
claims.quote: The Yucatec Maya were (and still are) speakers of the Yucatec language, and they settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica. Their chief god was the feathered serpent Kukulcan whose name means just that: feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan). He was a creator god, and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.

claims.statement: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds; the god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza, where a large temple was built in his honour.
claims.statement_id: Kukulcan dan wujud-wujud lainnya dipersatukan oleh keyakinan bahwa masing-masing dianggap dewa pencipta dan pembawa hujan serta angin. Sang dewa terutama dikaitkan dengan Chichen Itza, tempat kuil besar dibangun untuk menghormatinya.
claims.quote: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are all unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds. The god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza where a large temple was built in his honour.

claims.statement: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan, a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest, had some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE) come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.
claims.statement_id: Selain dewa Kukulcan, Maya Yucatec meyakini seorang pria bernama Kukulcan, pahlawan budaya yang berstatus penguasa atau pendeta, pada suatu waktu di abad ke-10 M (mungkin 987 M) datang ke atau bahkan mendirikan Chichen Itza di ujung utara semenanjung Yucatan.
claims.quote: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan - a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest - had, some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE), come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.

claims.statement: On the pyramid, a staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit with a small square structure of two chambers; three stairways have 91 steps and the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.
claims.statement_id: Pada piramida itu, sebuah tangga di tiap sisi naik melalui sembilan tingkat ke puncak dengan bangunan persegi kecil berisi dua ruang. Tiga tangga memiliki 91 anak tangga dan yang keempat 92, sehingga totalnya 365, satu untuk setiap hari dalam setahun.
claims.quote: A staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit where there is a small square structure consisting of two chambers. The pyramid is a marvel of architectural symmetry and design intention. Three stairways have 91 steps while the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.

claims.statement: The platform at the pyramid's top was used for religious ceremonies in honour of Kukulcan which included human sacrifices, a reminder that in Mesoamerican culture the gods had to be continuously fed and appeased to ensure the continuance and prosperity of the human race.
claims.statement_id: Pelataran di puncak piramida dipakai untuk upacara keagamaan menghormati Kukulcan yang mencakup pengorbanan manusia, pengingat bahwa dalam budaya Mesoamerika para dewa harus terus diberi makan dan ditenangkan demi kelangsungan dan kemakmuran umat manusia.
claims.quote: The platform at the pyramid's top was used for religious ceremonies in honour of Kukulcan which included human sacrifices, a reminder that in Mesoamerican culture the gods had to be continuously fed and appeased in order to ensure the continuance and prosperity of the human race.

claims.statement: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.
claims.statement_id: Ia diasosiasikan dengan langit malam, badai angin topan, obsidian, dan konflik.
claims.quote: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

claims.statement: He was considered one of the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap sebagai salah satu dari empat putra dewata primordial Ometecuhtli dan Omecihuatl.
claims.quote: He was considered one of the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity.

claims.statement: His main festival was Toxcatl, which, like most religious festivals of Aztec culture, involved human sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Festival utamanya adalah Toxcatl yang melibatkan pengorbanan manusia dalam budaya Aztec.
claims.quote: His main festival was Toxcatl, which, like most religious festivals of Aztec culture, involved human sacrifice.

claims.statement: Tezcatlipoca's nagual, his animal counterpart, was the jaguar.
claims.statement_id: Nagual atau rekan hewani Tezcatlipoca adalah seekor jaguar.
claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca's nagual, his animal counterpart, was the jaguar.

claims.statement: Tezcatlipoca, or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl, was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.
claims.statement_id: Tezcatlipoca atau 'Cermin Berasap' dalam bahasa Nahuatl adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik dan sangat penting bagi bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, terutama di Texcoco.
claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca (pron. Tez-ca-tli-po-ca) or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.

claims.statement: Tezcatlipoca was an invisible and omnipotent creator god, patron deity of warriors, and, as the bringer of both good and evil, the very embodiment of change through conflict.
claims.statement_id: Tezcatlipoca adalah dewa pencipta yang tak terlihat dan mahakuasa, dewa pelindung para prajurit, dan sebagai pembawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan ia adalah perwujudan perubahan melalui konflik.
claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca ... He was an invisible and omnipotent creator god, patron deity of warriors, and, as the bringer of both good and evil, he was the very embodiment of change through conflict.

claims.statement: Tezcatlipoca was the 10th of the 13 Lords of the Day and associated with the horned owl in the Mesoamerican calendar, while his nagual or animal spirit was the jaguar.
claims.statement_id: Tezcatlipoca adalah yang ke-10 dari 13 Penguasa Hari dan dikaitkan dengan burung hantu bertanduk dalam kalender Mesoamerika, sedangkan nagual atau roh hewannya adalah jaguar.
claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca was the 10th of the 13 Lords of the Day and associated with the horned owl in the Mesoamerican calendar whilst his nagual or animal spirit was the jaguar.

claims.statement: The Mesoamerican deity Tezcatlipoca was believed to be the son of the primordial androgynous god Ometeotl; in Aztec mythology he was the brother of Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec.
claims.statement_id: Tezcatlipoca diyakini putra dewa purba androgini Ometeotl; dalam mitologi Aztec ia saudara Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli, dan Xipe Totec.
claims.quote: The Mesoamerican deity Tezcatlipoca was believed to be the son of the primordial androgynous god Ometeotl. In Aztec mythology he was the brother of Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec.

claims.statement: In the Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl; the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun and, transformed into giant snakes, attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Mesoamerika dan Aztec, Tezcatlipoca menguasai dunia pertama Matahari tetapi digulingkan Quetzalcóatl. Keduanya kemudian bekerja sama menciptakan Matahari ke-5 dan, dengan berubah menjadi ular raksasa, menyerang dan memotong-motong monster reptil betina Tlaltecuhtli (atau Cipactli).
claims.quote: In the complex Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was then overthrown by Quetzalcóatl. The two later cooperated, however, to create the 5th Sun. Transformed into giant snakes, the two gods attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster known as Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli)

claims.statement: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth (or 5th) month of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies; an important part was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.
claims.statement_id: Pada bulan Tóxcatl, bulan keenam (atau kelima) tahun surya Aztec, Tezcatlipoca dipuja dalam upacara khusus; bagian penting upacara itu adalah peniruan sang dewa, paling sering oleh tawanan perang yang biasanya paling tampan dan paling berani.
claims.quote: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth month (or 5th) of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies. As with other Aztec religious rites an important part of the ceremony was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.

claims.statement: When the month came, the impersonator was dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival married his four goddesses; honoured with flowers and dances, the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was sacrificed and his heart removed with an obsidian knife to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.
claims.statement_id: Ketika bulan khusus itu tiba, sang peniru berpakaian prajurit dan dalam pesta pernikahan simbolis menikahi empat dewinya. Dihormati dengan bunga dan tarian, ia lalu dibawa ke kuil khusus tempat ia segera dikorbankan dan jantungnya diambil dengan pisau obsidian untuk menghormati Tezcatlipoca yang sejati.
claims.quote: When the special month finally came around the impersonator was handsomely dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival he married his four goddesses. Honoured with flowers and dances the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was promptly sacrificed and his heart removed using an obsidian knife in order to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

claims.statement: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli; he could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One', associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans).
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Biru, 'Penyihir Kolibri', dewa Tenochtitlán, tempat ia dikaitkan dengan matahari dan dewa perang Huitzilopochtli; ia bisa dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Merah, 'Si Terkuliti', yang dikaitkan dengan dewa Camaxtli dan Xipe Totec (dewa bangsa Tlaxcaltec).
claims.quote: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli. He could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One' and associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans)

claims.statement: The ever-present god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow; Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewa selalu hadir dan dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan; Tezcatlipoca bisa bermakna lebih suram ketika dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran.
claims.quote: Ever-present, the god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow. Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations when he was known as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction

claims.statement: Associated with conflict, he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli); he was not always protective to soldiers, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.
claims.statement_id: Dikaitkan dengan konflik, ia dikenal sebagai Yaotl atau 'Musuh' dan menjadi pelindung prajurit serta kamp pelatihan mereka (telpochcalli); namun ia tidak selalu melindungi prajurit, sebab kadang ia dapat ditemui di persimpangan jalan pada tengah malam, siap menantang prajurit yang lengah.
claims.quote: Also associated with conflict he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli). He was not always protective to soldiers, though, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

claims.statement: In later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan, sang dewa memiliki cermin obsidian hitam mengilap sebagai pengganti kaki kiri; pergantian kaki itu merujuk pada luka yang ia terima dalam pertempuran terkenalnya dengan Tlaltecuhtli saat Penciptaan.
claims.quote: in later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot. This replacement of the foot is a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

claims.statement: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake and sometimes carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering ditemani ular pirus dan kadang membawa empat anak panah di tangan kanannya, senjata yang ia pakai untuk menghukum pelaku kejahatan.
claims.quote: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake ... Sometimes he carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

claims.statement: The smoke from the couple's fire disturbed the stars, especially Citlallatonac and Citlalicue, who complained to Tezcatlipoca; he lopped off the heads of the couple and reattached them to their backsides, thus creating the very first dogs.
claims.statement_id: Asap api pasangan penyintas banjir mengganggu bintang-bintang, terutama Citlallatonac dan Citlalicue, yang mengeluh keras kepada Tezcatlipoca; ia memenggal kepala pasangan itu dan memasangnya di belakang tubuh mereka, sehingga lahirlah anjing-anjing pertama.
claims.quote: Then they decided to cook a fish but the smoke from their fire disturbed the stars, especially Citlallatonac and Citlalicue. These gods complained vociferously to Tezcatlipoca who, perhaps a little harshly, lopped off the heads of the couple and reattached them to their backsides, thus, the very first dogs were created.

claims.statement: One of the most famous art objects of the god is the decorated skull now in the British Museum in London, covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic with red thorny oyster shell in the nasal cavity.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu benda seni paling terkenal tentang sang dewa adalah tengkorak berhias yang kini ada di British Museum di London, dilapisi mosaik pirus dan lignit hitam dengan cangkang tiram berduri merah di rongga hidung.
claims.quote: one of the most famous art objects of the god is the decorated skull now in the British Museum in London. The skull is covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic with red thorny oyster shell in the nasal cavity.

claims.statement: With his lightning axe, Chaac strikes the clouds, causing them to produce thunder and rain.
claims.statement_id: Dengan kapak petirnya, Chaac menghantam awan sehingga menghasilkan guntur dan hujan.
claims.quote: With his lightning axe, Chaac strikes the clouds, causing them to produce thunder and rain.

claims.statement: Chaac corresponds to Tlaloc among the Aztecs and Cocijo among the Zapotecs.
claims.statement_id: Chaac sepadan dengan Tlaloc pada bangsa Aztec dan Cocijo pada bangsa Zapotec.
claims.quote: Chaac corresponds to Tlaloc among the Aztecs and Cocijo among the Zapotecs.

claims.statement: Four Chaacs are based in the cardinal directions and wear the directional colors.
claims.statement_id: Empat Chaac berdiam di empat arah mata angin dan mengenakan warna penjuru masing-masing.
claims.quote: Four Chaacs are based in the cardinal directions and wear the directional colors.

claims.statement: Contemporary Yucatec Maya farmers distinguish many more aspects of the rainfall and the clouds and personify them as different, hierarchically ordered rain deities.
claims.statement_id: Petani Maya Yucatec masa kini membedakan lebih banyak segi hujan dan awan serta mempersonifikasikannya sebagai dewa-dewa hujan yang berjenjang.
claims.quote: Contemporary Yucatec Maya farmers distinguish many more aspects of the rainfall and the clouds and personify them as different, hierarchically-ordered rain deities.

claims.statement: Chaac (also spelled Chac or, in Classic Mayan, Chaahk) is the name of the Maya god of rain, thunder, and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Chaac (juga ditulis Chac atau, dalam bahasa Maya Klasik, Chaahk) adalah nama dewa hujan, guntur, dan petir bangsa Maya.
claims.quote: Chaac (also spelled Chac or, in Classic Mayan, Chaahk ... is the name of the Maya god of rain, thunder, and lightning.

claims.statement: Chaac is usually depicted with a human body showing reptilian or amphibian scales and a non-human head with fangs and a long, pendulous nose; in the Classic style a shell is his ear ornament, and he often carries a shield and a lightning axe, the axe being personified by the closely related deity K'awiil, called Bolon Dzacab in Yucatec.
claims.statement_id: Chaac biasanya digambarkan bertubuh manusia dengan sisik reptil atau amfibi, berkepala bukan manusia dengan taring dan hidung panjang menggantung. Dalam gaya Klasik, cangkang menjadi hiasan telinganya. Ia sering membawa perisai dan kapak petir; kapak itu dipersonifikasikan oleh dewa yang berkerabat dekat, K'awiil, yang disebut Bolon Dzacab dalam bahasa Yucatec.
claims.quote: Chaac is usually depicted with a human body showing reptilian or amphibian scales, and with a non-human head evincing fangs and a long, pendulous nose. In the Classic style, a shell serves as his ear ornament. He often carries a shield and a lightning axe, the axe being personified by a closely related deity, K'awiil, called Bolon Dzacab in Yucatec.
