claims.statement: The rain deity is a patron of agriculture, and a well-known myth involving the Chaacs (or related rain and lightning deities) concerns the opening of the mountain where the maize was hidden.
claims.statement_id: Dewa hujan adalah pelindung pertanian. Mitos terkenal yang melibatkan para Chaac (atau dewa hujan dan petir terkait) adalah tentang terbukanya gunung tempat jagung disembunyikan.
claims.quote: The rain deity is a patron of agriculture. A well-known myth involving the Chaacs (or related rain and lightning deities) is about the opening of the mountain where the maize was hidden.

claims.statement: Classic period Maya sources also suggest that Chaac was the god who opened the mountain containing maize, using his lightning axe, K'awiil.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Maya masa Klasik juga menunjukkan bahwa Chaac adalah dewa yang membuka gunung berisi jagung dengan kapak petirnya, K'awiil.
claims.quote: Classic period Maya sources also suggest that Chaac was the god who opened the mountain containing maize, using his lightning axe, K'awiil.

claims.statement: Among the rituals for the rain deities, the Yucatec Chʼa Cháak ceremony for asking rain centers on a ceremonial banquet for the rain deities and includes four boys, one for each cardinal point, acting and chanting as frogs.
claims.statement_id: Di antara ritus bagi dewa-dewa hujan, upacara Chʼa Cháak orang Yucatec untuk memohon hujan berpusat pada jamuan seremonial bagi dewa hujan, dengan empat anak laki-laki (satu untuk tiap arah mata angin) yang berperan dan melantunkan seruan seperti katak.
claims.quote: Among the rituals for the rain deities, the Yucatec Chʼa Cháak ceremony for asking rain centers on a ceremonial banquet for the rain deities. It includes four boys (one for each cardinal point) acting and chanting as frogs.

claims.statement: Later, Chaac commits adultery with his brother's wife and is duly punished; his tears of agony give origin to the rain.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian Chaac berzina dengan istri saudaranya dan dihukum sepantasnya; air mata kesakitannya menjadi asal hujan.
claims.quote: Later, Chaac commits adultery with his brother's wife and is duly punished; his tears of agony give origin to the rain.

claims.statement: A large part of the Dresden Codex, one of the four surviving Maya codices, is dedicated to the Chaacs, their locations, and activities, and illustrates the intimate relationship between the Chaacs, the Bacabs, and the aged goddess Ixchel.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar salah satu dari empat kodeks Maya yang tersisa, Kodeks Dresden, dikhususkan bagi para Chaac, lokasi, dan kegiatan mereka. Kodeks itu memperlihatkan hubungan erat antara para Chaac, para Bacab, dan dewi tua Ixchel.
claims.quote: A large part of one of the four surviving Maya codices, the Dresden Codex, is dedicated to the Chaacs, their locations, and activities. It illustrates the intimate relationship existing between the Chaacs, the Bacabs, and the aged goddess, Ixchel.

claims.statement: Chaac continues to hold importance for some Maya groups in Mexico; in 2024 a statue of the Greek god Poseidon in Progreso, Yucatán, caused controversy among locals who found it offensive to their beliefs in Chaac.
claims.statement_id: Chaac tetap penting bagi sebagian kelompok Maya di Meksiko. Pada 2024, patung dewa Yunani Poseidon di Progreso, Yucatán, menimbulkan kontroversi di kalangan warga yang menganggapnya menyinggung kepercayaan mereka kepada Chaac.
claims.quote: Chaac continues to hold importance for some Maya groups in Mexico. In 2024, a statue of the Greek god Poseidon located in Progreso, Yucatán, caused controversy for locals who deemed it offensive to their beliefs in Chaac.

claims.statement: Chak (this source's spelling), the seeming counterpart of K'inich Ajaw, is the rain god or God B; part human and part reptile, he is usually shown with a lightning bolt, a serpent, or an axe.
claims.statement_id: Chak (ejaan sumber ini; ditulis Chaac di tempat lain), yang tampak sebagai padanan K'inich Ajaw, adalah dewa hujan atau Dewa B. Ia sebagian manusia dan sebagian reptil, dan biasanya ditampilkan dengan petir, ular, atau kapak.
claims.quote: Chak, the seeming counterpart of K'inich Ajaw, is the rain god or God B. Chak is both part human and part reptile and he is usually shown with a lightning bolt, a serpent, or an axe.

claims.statement: The Maya believe that Chak (this source's spelling) lived in caves where he would make lightning, thunder, and clouds.
claims.statement_id: Orang Maya percaya bahwa Chak (ejaan sumber ini) tinggal di gua tempat ia membuat petir, guntur, dan awan.
claims.quote: The Maya believe that Chak lived in caves where he would make lightning, thunder, and clouds.

claims.statement: Chak (this source's spelling) was both feared and worshipped; he brought needed rains but also produced floods and threatening lightning and behaved much like a wild storm, and demanded blood sacrifices in payment for the rains he provided.
claims.statement_id: Chak (ejaan sumber ini) ditakuti sekaligus disembah. Ia membawa hujan yang dibutuhkan orang, tetapi juga menimbulkan banjir dan petir yang mengancam, dan berperilaku seperti badai liar. Ia juga menuntut korban darah sebagai bayaran atas hujan yang ia berikan.
claims.quote: Chak, too, was both feared and worshipped. He brought the needed rains for the people, but also produced floods, threatening lightning, and behaved much like a wild storm. He also demanded blood sacrifices in payment for the rains that he provided.

claims.statement: In the Maya vocabulary of this source, Chaac (chác) means lightning, thunder, storm, rain, and is the generic name of the deities protecting waters and harvests.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kosakata Maya pada sumber ini, Chaac (chác) berarti petir, guntur, badai, dan hujan, dan merupakan nama umum bagi dewa-dewa pelindung perairan dan panen.
claims.quote: Chaac ou chác. s. foudre, tonnerre, orage, pluie;—nom générique des divinités protectrices des eaux et des moissons

claims.statement: Chac or Chaac was also the generic name of the gods protecting the countryside and harvests, like the tlaloque in Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Chac atau Chaac juga merupakan nama umum bagi dewa-dewa pelindung pedesaan dan panen, seperti tlaloque di Meksiko.
claims.quote: Chac ou Chaac, ainsi qu'on le verra plus loin, était aussi le nom générique des dieux protecteurs de la campagne et des moissons, comme les tlaloque au Mexique.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl was a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp, and also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp (pengantar jiwa). Ia juga dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan.
claims.quote: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl ... was a god of fire and lightning. He was commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and was a psychopomp. He was also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

claims.statement: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā; he is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star and was associated with heavenly fire.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl; keduanya putra Chīmalmā yang masih perawan. Ia adalah personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja (Evening Star) dan dikaitkan dengan api surgawi.
claims.quote: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā. He is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star, and was associated with heavenly fire.

claims.statement: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl, and his job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl disebut dewa kengerian (monstrosities) yang sinis dan mengenakan permata angin berbentuk kerang milik Quetzalcōātl. Tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like ehēcailacacōcatl "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl. His job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

claims.statement: Xolotl's empty eye sockets are explained by the Teotihuacan legend in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun; Xolotl withdrew from the sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.
claims.statement_id: Rongga matanya yang kosong dijelaskan dalam legenda Teotihuacan: ketika para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, Xolotl mundur dari pengorbanan itu dan menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
claims.quote: His empty eye sockets are explained in the legend of Teotihuacan, in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun. Xolotl withdrew from this sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claims.statement: Xolotl transformed himself into a young two-stalked maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and an amphibious animal (axolotl), and is thus a master transformer; in the end Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing him.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl mengubah dirinya menjadi tanaman jagung muda berbatang dua (xolotl), tanaman maguey ganda (mexolotl), dan hewan amfibi (axolotl), sehingga disebut ahli transformasi. Pada akhirnya Ehecatl berhasil menemukan dan membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Xolotl transformed himself into a young maize plant with two stalks (xolotl), a doubled maguey plant (mexolotl), and an amphibious animal (axolotl). Xolotl is thus a master transformer. In the end, Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing Xolotl.

claims.statement: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths; his two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle dog breed and the aquatic salamander known as the axolotl.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai psikopomp, Xolotl menuntun orang mati dalam perjalanan ke Mictlān, alam baka dalam mitos. Dua wujud hewan rohnya adalah anjing ras xoloitzcuintle dan salamander air yang disebut axolotl.
claims.quote: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths. His two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle breed of dog and the aquatic salamander species known as the axolotl.

claims.statement: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs, and is represented in codices, statuary, and other surviving Aztec art as a dog or a god with a dog's head.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl adalah dewa anjing bangsa Mexica, yang lazim dikenal sebagai Aztec. Dalam kodeks, arca, dan karya seni Aztec lain yang masih ada, ia digambarkan sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing.
claims.quote: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs. He is represented in codices, statuary, and other extant examples of Aztec art as a dog or a god with the head of a dog.

claims.statement: Although twins were generally seen as a bad omen in Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun kembar umumnya dianggap pertanda buruk dan dipandang dengan waswas dalam peradaban Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa pelindung kembar dan orang dengan kelainan fisik, yang menjadi bahan ketertarikan dalam budaya Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: While twins were generally seen as a bad omen and viewed with trepidation in the Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, which were a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

claims.statement: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl dalam misinya mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan umat manusia.
claims.quote: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity

claims.statement: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.
claims.statement_id: Ketika sebagian besar dewa rela mengorbankan diri, Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri.
claims.quote: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, setting a mythic precedent for the Aztec culture of human sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

claims.statement: Xolotl first tries to escape by turning into a double maize plant; when discovered he becomes a doubled maguey plant, and when that fails to conceal him he becomes a salamander still known by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl pertama kali mencoba kabur dengan menjadi tanaman jagung ganda. Ketika ketahuan, ia menjadi tanaman maguey ganda, dan ketika itu pun gagal menyembunyikannya, ia menjadi salamander yang hingga kini dikenal dengan nama Nahuatl axolotl.
claims.quote: Xolotl makes his first attempt to escape by turning into a double maize plant. When he is discovered in that guise, he turns into a doubled maguey plant, and when that transformation fails to conceal him, he turns into a salamander still known today by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

claims.statement: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Bahkan dalam wujud axolotl, Xolotl akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lainnya.
claims.quote: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods

claims.statement: Dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water.
claims.statement_id: Anjing, yang mungkin menjelmakan peran Xolotl, menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah setelah mati dan sangat berguna untuk menyeberangi perairan.
claims.quote: dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water

claims.statement: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl and atl, meaning "water", and so could be roughly translated as "water twin".
claims.statement_id: Kata axolotl adalah gabungan istilah Nahuatl xolotl dan atl yang berarti "air", sehingga kira-kira dapat diterjemahkan sebagai "kembar air".
claims.quote: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl (explained above) and atl, meaning "water," and so could be roughly translated as "water twin."

claims.statement: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog named Dante.
claims.statement_id: Penghormatan kepada Xolotl juga muncul dalam film Disney Coco (2017) berupa seekor anjing bernama Dante.
claims.quote: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog poignantly named Dante.

claims.statement: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame, which some scholars say symbolizes the Sun's perilous nighttime journey through the underworld; Xolotl can help the Sun's rebirth because he has the power to enter and exit the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Xolotl adalah pelindung permainan bola Mesoamerika. Sebagian sarjana berpendapat permainan itu melambangkan perjalanan malam Matahari yang berbahaya melalui dunia bawah; Xolotl dapat membantu kelahiran kembali Matahari karena ia berkuasa keluar-masuk dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame. Some scholars argue the ballgame symbolizes the Sun's perilous and uncertain nighttime journey through the underworld. Xolotl is able to help in the Sun's rebirth since he possesses the power to enter and exit the underworld.

claims.statement: Chalchiuhtlicue is associated with fertility, and she is the patroness of childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuhtlicue dikaitkan dengan kesuburan dan merupakan pelindung persalinan.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue is associated with fertility, and she is the patroness of childbirth.

claims.statement: Chalchiuhtlicue belongs to a larger group of Aztec rain gods, and she is closely related to the water god Chalchiuhtlatonal.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuhtlicue termasuk kelompok besar dewa hujan Aztec dan berkerabat dekat dengan dewa air Chalchiuhtlatonal.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue belongs to a larger group of Aztec rain gods, and she is closely related to the water god Chalchiuhtlatonal.

claims.statement: In Aztec religion, Chalchiuitlicue (a variant spelling of Chalchiuhtlicue) helps Tlaloc to rule the paradisial kingdom of Tlalocan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Aztec, Chalchiuitlicue (ejaan lain dari Chalchiuhtlicue) membantu Tlaloc memerintah kerajaan firdaus Tlalocan.
claims.quote: In Aztec religion, Chalchiuitlicue helps Tlaloc to rule the paradisial kingdom of Tlalocan.

claims.statement: Chalchiutlicue (a variant spelling) brings fertility to crops and is thought to protect women and children.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiutlicue (ejaan lain) membawa kesuburan bagi tanaman dan diyakini melindungi perempuan dan anak-anak.
claims.quote: Chalchiutlicue brings fertility to crops and is thought to protect women and children.

claims.statement: Chalchiuitlicue was the wife or sister of the rain god Tlaloc depending on the text; she was also the mother of the moon god Tecciztecatl, and in other texts the wife of Xiuhtecuhtli, a senior Aztec deity.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuitlicue adalah istri atau saudari dewa hujan Aztec Tlaloc, tergantung teksnya. Ia juga ibu dewa bulan Tecciztecatl, dan dalam teks lain ia istri Xiuhtecuhtli, dewa senior Aztec.
claims.quote: Chalchiuitlicue was the wife or sister of the Aztec god of rain Tlaloc, depending on the text. ... She was also the mother of the Aztec moon god Tecciztecatl. In other texts, she was the wife of Xiuhtecuhtli, who was a senior deity for the Aztecs.

claims.statement: Chalchiuitlicue literally translates to "Jade her skirt", though the name is most commonly read as "she of the jade skirt"; she was also known as Chalchiuhtlatonac, "She who shines like jade", and, to the Tlaxcalans, Matlalcueye, "Possessor of the Blue Skirt".
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuitlicue secara harfiah berarti "Jade roknya", tetapi namanya paling lazim ditafsirkan sebagai "dia yang berok batu giok". Ia juga dikenal sebagai Chalchiuhtlatonac, "dia yang bersinar seperti batu giok", dan oleh bangsa Tlaxcala disebut Matlalcueye, "pemilik rok biru".
claims.quote: Chalchiuitlicue directly translates to 'Jade her skirt'; however, her name is most commonly interpreted as 'she of the jade skirt'. She was also known as Chalchiuhtlatonac ... 'She who shines like jade' and Matlalcueye 'Possessor of the Blue Skirt' by the Tlaxcalans

claims.statement: In the Aztec Five Suns creation myth, Chalchiuhtlicue presided over the Fourth Sun; she is believed to have retaliated against Tlaloc's mistreatment by releasing 52 years of rain, causing a giant flood that destroyed the Fourth Sun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Lima Matahari Aztec, Chalchiuhtlicue memimpin Matahari Keempat. Diyakini ia membalas perlakuan buruk Tlaloc dengan melepaskan hujan selama 52 tahun, menimbulkan banjir besar yang menghancurkan Matahari Keempat.
claims.quote: In the Aztec creation myth of the Five Suns, Chalchiuhtlicue presided over the Fourth Sun or the fourth creation of the world. It is believed that Chalchiuhtlicue retaliated against Tlaloc's mistreatment of her by releasing 52 years of rain, causing a giant flood which caused the Fourth Sun to be destroyed.

claims.statement: In addition to water-related deaths, Chalchiuhtlicue presided over birth rituals, the bathing of sacrificial victims and ceremonial actors, judicial purification, royal investiture, and the recycling of ritual waste.
claims.statement_id: Selain kematian yang berkaitan dengan air, Chalchiuhtlicue memimpin ritus kelahiran, pemandian korban persembahan dan pelaku upacara, penyucian peradilan, penobatan raja, dan pendaurulangan limbah ritual.
claims.quote: In addition to water-related deaths, Chalchiuhtlicue presided over birth rituals, bathing of sacrificial victims and ceremonial actors, judiciary purification, royal investiture, and the recycling of ritual waste.

claims.statement: Chalchiutlicue (a variant spelling) was the guardian of children and newborns; when children fell ill, healers called on the goddess while practicing hydromancy to find the tonalli (spirits) of the sick children.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiutlicue (ejaan lain) adalah penjaga anak-anak dan bayi baru lahir. Ketika anak jatuh sakit, para tabib memanggil sang dewi sambil melakukan hidromansi untuk menemukan tonalli (roh) anak yang sakit.
claims.quote: Chalchiutlicue was the guardian of the children and newborns. When children fell ill, healers called on the goddess as they practiced hydromancy in order to find the tonalli (spirits) of sick children.

claims.statement: When represented in sculpture, Chalchiutlicue (a variant spelling) is often carved from green stone in accordance with her name.
claims.statement_id: Bila diwujudkan dalam patung, Chalchiutlicue (ejaan lain) sering dipahat dari batu hijau sesuai dengan namanya.
claims.quote: When represented through sculpture, Chalchiutlicue is often carved from green stone in accordance with her name.

claims.statement: Chalchiuhtlicue was the Aztec goddess of lakes and streams, related to the liquid environment of the womb and important in ceremonies related to birth.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuhtlicue adalah dewi danau dan aliran air bangsa Aztec. Ia dikaitkan dengan lingkungan cair rahim dan berperan penting dalam upacara kelahiran.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue was the Aztec goddess of lakes and streams. She was related to the liquid environment of the womb and played an important role in ceremonies related to birth.

claims.statement: In the picture a stream issues from beneath the goddess carrying two small humans, likely infants, and seashells at the water's edge indicate Chalchiuhtlicue's association with fertility.
claims.statement_id: Pada gambar itu, aliran air keluar dari bawah sang dewi dan membawa dua manusia kecil, kemungkinan bayi. Cangkang kerang di tepi air menunjukkan kaitan Chalchiuhtlicue dengan kesuburan.
claims.quote: In this image, a stream issues from beneath the goddess with two small humans, likely infants, carried up in the waters. There are seashells at the edges of the water, indicating Chalchiuhtlicue's association with fertility.

claims.statement: In the source's section on Chalchihuitlicue (its spelling), the goddess was the wife of Tlaloc, god of rain and moisture; the name means Lady of the Emerald Robe, alluding to the colour of water, and she was specially worshipped by water-carriers and all whose work brought them into contact with water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bagian tentang Chalchihuitlicue (ejaan sumber), sang dewi adalah istri Tlaloc, dewa hujan dan kelembapan. Namanya berarti "Nyonya Jubah Zamrud", merujuk warna unsur air yang sebagian dikuasainya. Ia dipuja khusus oleh para pembawa air dan semua orang yang pekerjaannya bersentuhan dengan air.
claims.quote: Chalchihuitlicue This goddess was the wife of Tlaloc, the god of rain and moisture. The name means Lady of the Emerald Robe, in allusion to the colour of the element over which the deity partly presided. She was specially worshipped by the water-carriers of Mexico, and all those whose avocation brought them into contact with water.

claims.statement: The priests of Tlaloc plunged into a lake imitating the sounds and movements of frogs, which were under the god's special protection; Chalchihuitlicue (the source's spelling), his wife, was often symbolised by a small image of a frog.
claims.statement_id: Para imam Tlaloc menyelam ke danau sambil menirukan suara dan gerak katak, yang sebagai penghuni air berada di bawah perlindungan khusus sang dewa. Chalchihuitlicue (ejaan sumber), istrinya, sering dilambangkan dengan gambar kecil seekor katak.
claims.quote: the priests of Tlaloc plunged into a lake, imitating the sounds and movements of frogs, which, as denizens of water, were under the special protection of the god. Chalchihuitlicue, his wife, was often symbolised by the small image of a frog.

claims.statement: According to myths, Chalchiuhtlicue once ate the sun and the moon, and she is often associated with serpents, as most Aztec water deities are.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos, Chalchiuhtlicue pernah memakan matahari dan bulan. Ia sering dikaitkan dengan ular, seperti kebanyakan dewa air Aztec.
claims.quote: According to myths, Chalchiuhtlicue once ate the sun and the moon. She is often associated with serpents, as most Aztec water deities are.

claims.statement: Five of the 20 big celebrations in the Aztec calendar were dedicated to Chalchiutlicue (a variant spelling) and her husband (or brother) Tlaloc, when priests dove into a lake and imitated frogs, hoping to bring rain.
claims.statement_id: Lima dari 20 perayaan besar dalam kalender Aztec dipersembahkan bagi Chalchiutlicue (ejaan lain) dan suaminya (atau saudaranya) Tlaloc. Pada perayaan itu para imam menyelam ke danau dan menirukan gerak serta suara katak untuk memohon hujan.
claims.quote: Five of the 20 big celebrations in the Aztec calendar were dedicated to Chalchiutlicue and her husband (or brother) Tlaloc. During these celebrations, priests dove into a lake and imitated the movements and the croaking of frogs, hoping to bring rain.

claims.statement: Paul Bunyan is a giant lumberjack and folk hero in American and Canadian folklore; his tall tales revolve around his superhuman labors, and he is customarily accompanied by Babe the Blue Ox, his pet and working animal.
claims.statement_id: Paul Bunyan adalah penebang kayu raksasa dan pahlawan rakyat dalam cerita rakyat Amerika dan Kanada. Cerita-cerita bualannya berkisar pada kerja-kerja supermanusiawinya, dan ia biasanya ditemani Babe si Sapi Biru, hewan peliharaan sekaligus hewan kerjanya.
claims.quote: Paul Bunyan is a giant lumberjack and folk hero in American and Canadian folklore. His tall tales revolve around his superhuman labors, and he is customarily accompanied by Babe the Blue Ox (French: Babe le bœuf bleu ), his pet and working animal.

claims.statement: According to this source the character first appeared in print in 1893 but originated earlier in the oral tradition of North American loggers.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini pertama kali muncul di media cetak pada 1893 menurut sumber ini, tetapi berasal lebih awal dari tradisi lisan para penebang kayu Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: Paul Bunyan is a giant lumberjack and folk hero in American and Canadian folklore. ... The character first appeared in print in 1893 but originated earlier in the oral tradition of North American loggers.

claims.statement: Several researchers have attempted to trace Paul Bunyan to the character of Bon Jean of French Canadian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa peneliti berusaha menelusuri Paul Bunyan ke tokoh Bon Jean dalam cerita rakyat Kanada Prancis.
claims.quote: Several researchers have attempted to trace Paul Bunyan to the character of Bon Jean of French Canadian folklore.

claims.statement: In contrast to the lengthy narratives abundant in published material, Paul Bunyan "stories" told in lumbercamp bunkhouses were short fragments, some including motifs from older folktales such as absurdly severe weather and fearsome critters.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari narasi panjang dalam bahan terbitan, "cerita" Paul Bunyan yang dituturkan di barak kamp penebangan disajikan dalam potongan pendek. Sebagian cerita itu memuat motif dari dongeng lama, seperti cuaca yang sangat buruk dan makhluk menakutkan (fearsome critters).
claims.quote: In contrast to the lengthy narratives abundant in published material, Paul Bunyan "stories" when told in the lumbercamp bunkhouses were presented in short fragments. Some of these stories include motifs from older folktales, such as absurdly severe weather and fearsome critters.

claims.statement: Paul Bunyan was more widely popularized by freelance writer William B. Laughead (1882–1958) in a 1916 promotional pamphlet for the Red River Lumber Company.
claims.statement_id: Paul Bunyan lebih luas dipopulerkan oleh penulis lepas William B. Laughead (1882–1958) lewat pamflet promosi tahun 1916 untuk Red River Lumber Company.
claims.quote: Paul Bunyan was more widely popularized by freelance writer William B. Laughead (1882–1958) in a 1916 promotional pamphlet for the Red River Lumber Company.

claims.statement: Among other things Laughead named the blue ox "Babe", created the first pictorial representation of Bunyan, and raised Paul Bunyan's height to impossible proportions (towering over trees in his version, whereas in earlier folktales Bunyan was extraordinarily tall and strong but of human proportions).
claims.statement_id: Antara lain, Laughead memberi nama "Babe" pada sapi biru, membuat gambar pertama Bunyan, dan menambah tinggi Paul Bunyan hingga mustahil (dalam versi Laughead ia menjulang melampaui pepohonan, sedangkan dalam dongeng lebih awal Bunyan sangat tinggi dan kuat tetapi berukuran manusia).
claims.quote: Among other things, Laughead gave the name "Babe" to the blue ox, created the first pictorial representation of Bunyan, and increased Paul Bunyan's height to impossible proportions (in Laughead's version, Paul Bunyan towers over trees, while in the earlier folktales Bunyan had been extraordinarily tall and strong, but of human proportions).

claims.statement: Laughead attributes the creation of several American landscapes, landmarks, and natural wonders to Paul Bunyan, writing that Paul Bunyan and Babe are said to have created the 10,000 lakes of Minnesota with their footprints.
claims.statement_id: Laughead mengaitkan terciptanya beberapa lanskap, tengara, dan keajaiban alam Amerika dengan Paul Bunyan. Ia menulis bahwa Paul Bunyan dan Babe dikatakan menciptakan 10.000 danau Minnesota lewat jejak kaki mereka.
claims.quote: Laughead attributes the creation of several American landscapes, landmarks and natural wonders to Paul Bunyan. He wrote that Paul Bunyan and Babe are said to have created the 10,000 lakes of Minnesota by their footprints.

claims.statement: Stories about Bunyan credited him with creating the Grand Canyon by pulling his ax behind him and Mount Hood by putting stones on his campfire.
claims.statement_id: Cerita tentang Bunyan menyebut ia menciptakan Grand Canyon dengan menyeret kapaknya di belakangnya, dan Mount Hood dengan menumpuk batu di atas api unggunnya.
claims.quote: Stories about Bunyan credited him with creating the Grand Canyon by pulling his ax behind him, and Mount Hood by putting stones on his campfire.

claims.statement: The first known reference to Paul Bunyan in print appeared in the March 17, 1893, issue of the Gladwin County Record.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan tercetak pertama yang diketahui tentang Paul Bunyan muncul dalam terbitan 17 Maret 1893 Gladwin County Record.
claims.quote: The first known reference of Paul Bunyan in print appeared in the March 17, 1893, issue of Gladwin County Record.

claims.statement: In all the articles Paul Bunyan is praised as a logger of great physical strength and unrivaled skill.
claims.statement_id: Dalam semua artikel itu, Paul Bunyan dipuji sebagai penebang kayu bertenaga fisik besar dan berketerampilan tiada banding.
claims.quote: In all the articles, Paul Bunyan is praised as a logger of great physical strength and unrivaled skill.

claims.statement: The figure of Bunyan was adapted by the Ojibwe people into folklore about Nanabozho, a culture hero of the Ojibwe and Anishinaabe.
claims.statement_id: Sosok Bunyan diadaptasi orang Ojibwe menjadi cerita rakyat tentang Nanabozho, pahlawan budaya orang Ojibwe dan Anishinaabe.
claims.quote: The figure of Bunyan was adapted by the Ojibwe people into folklore about Nanabozho, a culture hero of the Ojibwe and Anishinaabe.

claims.statement: There are many hypotheses about the etymology of the name Paul Bunyan, and much of the commentary focuses on a French-Canadian origin for the name.
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak hipotesis tentang asal-usul nama Paul Bunyan. Sebagian besar ulasan berfokus pada asal Prancis-Kanada bagi nama itu.
claims.quote: There are many hypotheses about the etymology of the name Paul Bunyan. Much of the commentary focuses on a French-Canadian origin for the name.

claims.statement: The camp joke is a series of imaginative tales about the year Paul Bunyan lumbered in North Dakota, in which the great Paul gets out countless millions of timber in the year of the "blue snow".
claims.statement_id: Lelucon andalannya, yang pasti dipakai untuk menguji orang baru di kamp, berupa serangkaian cerita khayal tentang tahun ketika Paul Bunyan menebang kayu di North Dakota. Sang Paul digambarkan menghasilkan jutaan kayu pada tahun "salju biru".
claims.quote: His pet joke and the one with which the green horn at the camp is sure to be tried, consists of a series of imaginative tales about the year Paul Bunyan lumbered in North Dakota. The great Paul is represented as getting out countless millions of timber in the year of the "blue snow".

claims.statement: According to this source Paul Bunyan first appeared in print in 1906 but languished in relative obscurity until Laughead's efforts for the Red River advertising campaign.
claims.statement_id: Paul Bunyan pertama kali muncul di media cetak pada 1906 menurut sumber ini, tetapi tetap relatif tak dikenal sampai upaya Laughead untuk kampanye iklan Red River.
claims.quote: Paul Bunyan first appeared in print in 1906 but languished in relative obscurity until Laughead's efforts for the Red River advertising campaign.

claims.statement: Finally Walker suggested the folk hero Paul Bunyan, stories of whom circulated in forestry camps, especially in the Great Lakes region.
claims.statement_id: Akhirnya Walker mengusulkan pahlawan rakyat Paul Bunyan, yang ceritanya beredar di kamp-kamp kehutanan, terutama di kawasan Great Lakes.
claims.quote: Finally, Walker suggested the folk hero Paul Bunyan, stories of whom circulated forestry camps, especially in the Great Lakes region.

claims.statement: Through his text and illustrations Laughead made significant contributions to the Bunyan canon, developing new characters including Babe the Blue Ox and Babe's custodian Brimstone Bill, and bringing minor characters into focus such as the penny-pinching clerk Johnny Inkslinger and camp cook Big Joe.
claims.statement_id: Lewat teks dan ilustrasinya, Laughead menyumbang banyak pada kanon Bunyan, termasuk menciptakan tokoh baru seperti Babe si Sapi Biru dan pengasuhnya Brimstone Bill, serta menonjolkan tokoh kecil seperti juru tulis pelit Johnny Inkslinger dan juru masak kamp Big Joe.
claims.quote: Through his text and illustrations, Laughead made significant contributions to the Bunyan canon ... developing wholly new characters, including Babe the Blue Ox and Babe's custodian Brimstone Bill; and bringing minor characters into distincition, including the penny-pinching clerk Johnny Inkslinger and camp cooks Big Joe.

claims.statement: As the tall tales spread coast to coast, Paul the Lumberjack-Hero was dwarfed by Paul the American Spirit; no longer restricted to the woods, Paul Bunyan became a legend of all regions, credited with deeds from digging Puget Sound to succeeding as a Southwest oilman to building the Panama Canal.
claims.statement_id: Ketika cerita bualan itu meluas dari pantai ke pantai, Paul Sang Pahlawan Penebang Kayu terkalahkan oleh Paul Sang Semangat Amerika. Tak lagi terbatas di hutan, Paul Bunyan menjadi legenda semua kawasan. Cerita menyebut penebang itu menggali Puget Sound, sukses sebagai pengusaha minyak di Barat Daya, hingga membangun Terusan Panama.
claims.quote: As the tall tales stretched coast to coast, Paul the Lumberjack-Hero was dwarfed by Paul the American Spirit. No longer restricted to the woods, Paul Bunyan became a legend of all regions. Stories credited the lumberman with varied accomplishments, from digging the Puget Sound to succeeding as a Southwest oilman to building the Panama Canal.

claims.statement: The company officially adopted Paul Bunyan's name for use in its business dealings and copyrighted Laughead's illustration of Paul Bunyan's head, using it as a trademark for its products.
claims.statement_id: Perusahaan itu secara resmi memakai nama Paul Bunyan dalam urusan bisnisnya dan mendaftarkan hak cipta ilustrasi kepala Paul Bunyan karya Laughead, memakainya sebagai merek dagang produknya.
claims.quote: The company officially adopted Paul Bunyan's name for use in its business dealings and copyrighted Laughead's illustration of Paul Bunyan's head, using it as a trademark for its products.

claims.statement: A postcard-sized booklet, Introducing Mr. Paul Bunyan of Westwood, California, was published in 1914, and its companion, Tales About Paul Bunyan, Volume II, was printed two years later.
claims.statement_id: Buklet seukuran kartu pos Introducing Mr. Paul Bunyan of Westwood, California terbit pada 1914, dan pasangannya Tales About Paul Bunyan, Volume II dicetak dua tahun kemudian.
claims.quote: A postcard-sized booklet Introducing Mr. Paul Bunyan of Westwood, California was published in 1914, and its companion Tales About Paul Bunyan, Volume II was printed just two years later.

claims.statement: In 1922 the company published The Marvelous Exploits of Paul Bunyan, a re-vamped version of Laughead's first work.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1922 perusahaan itu menerbitkan The Marvelous Exploits of Paul Bunyan, versi yang dirombak dari karya pertama Laughead.
claims.quote: In 1922, the company published The Marvelous Exploits of Paul Bunyan, a re-vamped version of Laughead's first work.

claims.statement: The Ogopogo is a lake monster said to inhabit Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, Canada, in Canadian folklore, and some scholars have traced its development from First Nations folklore and widespread water-monster motifs.
claims.statement_id: Ogopogo adalah monster danau yang dikatakan mendiami Danau Okanagan di British Columbia, Kanada, dalam cerita rakyat Kanada. Sebagian sarjana menelusuri perkembangan makhluk ini dari cerita rakyat First Nations dan motif umum monster air.
claims.quote: The Ogopogo is a lake monster said to inhabit Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, Canada in Canadian folklore. Some scholars have charted the entity's development from First Nations folklore and widespread water monster folklore motifs.

claims.statement: Okanagan Lake is the largest of five inter-connected freshwater fjord lakes in the Okanagan Valley, named after the Syilx Okanagan Nation who have lived there since time immemorial, and created when melting glaciers flooded a valley 10,000 years ago.
claims.statement_id: Danau Okanagan adalah yang terbesar dari lima danau fyord air tawar yang saling terhubung di Lembah Okanagan, British Columbia. Dinamai menurut Bangsa Syilx Okanagan yang telah mendiami lembah itu sejak zaman purba, danau ini terbentuk ketika gletser yang mencair membanjiri sebuah lembah 10.000 tahun lalu.
claims.quote: Okanagan Lake is the largest of five inter-connected freshwater fjord lakes in the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia. Named after the Syilx Okanagan Nation that have lived in the valley since time immemorial, it was created when melting glaciers flooded a valley 10,000 years ago.

claims.statement: The lake monster has mostly been described as a serpentine creature with smooth dark skin and a large body thicker than a telephone pole, up to 15 m (49 ft) long.
claims.statement_id: Monster danau ini kebanyakan digambarkan sebagai makhluk menyerupai ular berkulit gelap licin dengan tubuh besar lebih tebal daripada tiang telepon dan panjang hingga 15 m.
claims.quote: The lake monster has been mostly described as being a serpentine creature with smooth dark skin with a large body thicker than a telephone pole and being up to 15 m (49 ft) in length.

claims.statement: The Naitaka was often described as using its tail to create fierce storms to drown victims.
claims.statement_id: Naitaka kerap digambarkan memakai ekornya untuk menimbulkan badai dahsyat guna menenggelamkan korban.
claims.quote: The Naitaka was often described as using its tail to create fierce storms to drown victims.

claims.statement: The monster is said to move at incredible speeds, coiling its body in vertical undulations and propelling itself with a powerful tail.
claims.statement_id: Monster itu dikatakan bergerak dengan kecepatan luar biasa, melingkarkan tubuhnya dalam gelombang vertikal, dan melaju dengan ekornya yang kuat.
claims.quote: The monster has said to move at incredible speeds, coiling its body in vertical undulations, and propelling itself with a powerful tail.

claims.statement: According to historian Mark M. Orkin the creature received its colonial name "on a night in 1924 when the strains of an English music-hall song were first heard in the city of Vernon, British Columbia", and the song lines he cites end "And Ogopogo was his name".
claims.statement_id: Menurut sejarawan Mark M. Orkin, makhluk ini menerima nama kolonialnya "pada suatu malam tahun 1924 ketika alunan lagu music-hall Inggris pertama kali terdengar di kota Vernon, British Columbia"; larik lagu yang ia kutip diakhiri "And Ogopogo was his name".
claims.quote: According to historian Mark M. Orkin, the creature received its colonial name "on a night in 1924 when the strains of an English music-hall song were first heard in the city of Vernon, British Columbia". Orkin cites the following lines from the song: ... And Ogopogo was his name.

claims.statement: According to Ben Radford the Ogopogo is "more closely tied to native myths than is any other lake monster"; the Secwepemc and Syilx natives regarded it, calling it the Naitaka, as "an evil supernatural entity with great power and ill intent".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ben Radford, Ogopogo "lebih erat terikat pada mitos pribumi daripada monster danau mana pun". Orang Secwepemc dan Syilx menganggap Ogopogo, yang mereka sebut Naitaka, sebagai "entitas gaib jahat dengan kekuatan besar dan niat buruk".
claims.quote: According to Ben Radford, the Ogopogo is "more closely tied to native myths than is any other lake monster." The Secwepemc and Syilx natives regarded the Ogopogo, which they called the Naitaka, as "an evil supernatural entity with great power and ill intent."

claims.statement: In native lore Naitaka demanded a live sacrifice for safe crossing of the lake, and for hundreds of years First Nations would sacrifice small animals before entering the water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi pribumi, Naitaka menuntut persembahan hidup agar penyeberangan danau aman. Selama ratusan tahun, orang First Nations mengorbankan hewan kecil sebelum memasuki air.
claims.quote: In native lore, Naitaka demanded a live sacrifice for safe crossing of the lake. For hundreds of years, First Nations would sacrifice small animals before entering the water.

claims.statement: Oral traditions often described the visiting chief Timbasket, who rejected the required sacrifice and denied the demon's existence; when he entered the lake by canoe with his family, Naitaka "whipped up the surface of the lake with his long tail" and the canoe and its occupants were sucked to the bottom.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan sering menceritakan kepala suku tamu Timbasket yang menolak persembahan yang disyaratkan dan menyangkal keberadaan iblis itu. Ketika ia memasuki danau dengan kano bersama keluarganya, Naitaka "mencambuk permukaan danau dengan ekor panjangnya" dan kano beserta penumpangnya terhisap ke dasar danau.
claims.quote: Oral traditions often described visiting chief Timbasket, who rejected the required sacrifice, denying the existence of the demon. Upon entering the lake on a canoe with his family, Naitaka "whipped up the surface of the lake with his long tail" and the canoe and its occupants were sucked to the bottom of the lake.

claims.statement: According to Pat Raphael of the Westbank First Nation, the demonic view of Naitaka arose from miscommunication between early European settlers and the Syilx/Okanagan people; to the Syilx it is a sacred spirit of the lake that protects the valley.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Pat Raphael dari Westbank First Nation, pandangan yang menganggap Naitaka iblis muncul dari salah komunikasi antara pemukim Eropa awal di Kanada dan orang Syilx/Okanagan. Bagi orang Syilx, ia adalah roh suci danau yang melindungi lembah.
claims.quote: According to Pat Raphael of the Westbank First Nation, a member nation of the larger Okanagan Nation Alliance, the demonic view of Naitaka came about through miscommunication between Canada's early European settlers and the Syilx/Okanagan people. To the Syilx, it's ... a sacred spirit of the lake that protects the valley.

claims.statement: Jordan Coble of the Westbank First Nation counters that the creature is a being meant to be respected, not feared.
claims.statement_id: Namun Jordan Coble dari Westbank First Nation menyanggah dengan mengatakan bahwa makhluk itu adalah sosok yang dimaksudkan untuk dihormati, bukan ditakuti.
claims.quote: However, Jordan Coble of the Westbank First Nation counters by saying that the creature is a being that is meant to be both respected, not feared.

claims.statement: The Naitaka was often described as using its tail to create fierce storms to drown victims; in 1855 settler John MacDougal claimed his horses were sucked down into the water, and nearly his canoe before he cut the line.
claims.statement_id: Naitaka kerap digambarkan memakai ekornya untuk menimbulkan badai dahsyat guna menenggelamkan korban. Pada 1855, pemukim John MacDougal mengaku kudanya terhisap ke dalam air, dan hampir kanonya sebelum ia memotong talinya.
claims.quote: The Naitaka was often described as using its tail to create fierce storms to drown victims. In 1855, settler John MacDougal claimed that his horses were sucked down into the water, and nearly his canoe before he cut the line.

claims.statement: In the 1980s a local tourism agency offered a cash reward for a proven sighting of the beast, and Greenpeace announced it must be filmed and not captured, listing the Ogopogo as an endangered species.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1980-an, sebuah lembaga pariwisata setempat menawarkan hadiah uang tunai bagi penampakan makhluk itu yang terbukti. Greenpeace menyatakan makhluk itu harus difilmkan dan tidak ditangkap: Ogopogo didaftarkan sebagai spesies terancam.
claims.quote: In the 1980s, a local tourism agency offered a cash reward for a proven sighting of the beast. Greenpeace announced that the beast must be filmed and not captured: the Ogopogo was listed as an endangered species.

claims.statement: In 2011 a cell phone video captured two dark shapes in the water; a suggested explanation is that it shows two logs.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2011, sebuah video ponsel merekam dua bentuk gelap di air. Penjelasan yang diajukan adalah bahwa video itu menunjukkan dua batang kayu.
claims.quote: In 2011, a cell phone video captured two dark shapes in the water. A suggested explanation is that the video shows two logs.

claims.statement: Ogopogo is a legendary lake monster said to live in Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, and stories of a large creature in the lake go back hundreds of years, told by the region's First Nations people who believed it to be a sacred lake spirit.
claims.statement_id: Ogopogo adalah nama monster danau legendaris yang dikatakan hidup di Danau Okanagan di provinsi British Columbia, Kanada. Kisah tentang makhluk besar di danau itu sudah berusia ratusan tahun dan dituturkan orang First Nations setempat yang meyakininya sebagai roh danau yang suci.
claims.quote: Ogopogo is the name of a legendary lake monster that is said to live in Okanagan Lake in the Canadian province of British Columbia. Stories of a large creature living in the lake go back hundreds of years and were told by the region’s First Nations people who believed it to be a sacred lake spirit.

claims.statement: While eyewitness accounts vary, most describe Ogopogo as a snake-like creature about 80 feet (24 meters) long with a head resembling a horse or a goat.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun kesaksian berbeda-beda, kebanyakan menggambarkan Ogopogo sebagai makhluk menyerupai ular sepanjang sekitar 80 kaki (24 meter) dengan kepala mirip kuda atau kambing.
claims.quote: While eyewitness accounts vary, most describe Ogopogo as a snake-like creature about 80-feet (24-meters) long with a head resembling a horse or a goat.

claims.statement: To the Syilx the creature was known as N'ha-a-itk, meaning "sacred spirit of the lake", said to be dark with the head of a horse and the antlers of a deer, and according to local legend a spirit that could also take physical form.
claims.statement_id: Bagi orang Syilx, makhluk itu dikenal sebagai N'ha-a-itk, yang berarti "roh suci danau". N'ha-a-itk dikatakan berwarna gelap dengan kepala kuda dan tanduk rusa. Menurut legenda setempat, N'ha-a-itk adalah roh yang juga dapat mengambil wujud fisik.
claims.quote: To the Syilx, the creature was known as N’ha-a-itk, which means “sacred spirit of the lake.” N’ha-a-itk was said to be dark in color with the head of a horse and the antlers of a deer. According to local legend, N’ha-a-itk was a spirit that could also take physical form.

claims.statement: It was said to live in a cave near an island and required a sacrifice for safe passage on the lake; people were said to bring chickens, salmon, and other small animals to toss into the lake to appease N'ha-a-itk.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu dikatakan tinggal di gua dekat sebuah pulau dan menuntut persembahan agar penyeberangan danau aman. Orang-orang dikatakan membawa ayam, salmon, dan hewan kecil lain untuk dilemparkan ke danau guna menenangkan N'ha-a-itk.
claims.quote: It was said to live in a cave near an island and required a sacrifice to allow the safe passage of the lake. The people were said to bring chickens, salmon, and other small animals with them to toss into the lake to appease N’ha-a-itk.

claims.statement: The first recorded sighting by a settler occurred in 1855, when a man claimed something dragged his horses underwater as he tried to cross the lake; in 1872 a Canadian author, Susan Allison, reported seeing a dinosaur swimming in Okanagan Lake.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan pertama yang tercatat oleh seorang pemukim terjadi pada 1855, ketika seorang pria mengaku ada sesuatu yang menyeret kudanya ke bawah air saat ia menyeberangi danau. Pada 1872, penulis Kanada bernama Susan Allison melaporkan melihat seekor dinosaurus berenang di Danau Okanagan.
claims.quote: The first recorded sighting by a settler occurred in 1855, when a man claimed that something dragged his horses underwater as he tried to cross the lake. In 1872, a Canadian author named Susan Allison reported that she saw a dinosaur swimming in Okanagan Lake.

claims.statement: In the 1920s local tourism officials decided to call the creature Ogopogo, a name taken from a popular English folk song, The Ogo-Pogo.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1920-an, pejabat pariwisata setempat memutuskan menamai makhluk itu Ogopogo, nama yang diambil dari lagu rakyat Inggris populer The Ogo-Pogo.
claims.quote: In the 1920s, local tourism officials decided to call the creature Ogopogo, a name taken from a popular English folk song The Ogo-Pogo.

claims.statement: During the 1980s an Okanagan Lake tourism association offered a one-million-dollar reward for anyone who could provide "living proof" that Ogopogo really existed.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1980-an, sebuah asosiasi pariwisata Danau Okanagan menawarkan hadiah satu juta dolar bagi siapa pun yang dapat memberikan "bukti hidup" bahwa Ogopogo benar-benar ada.
claims.quote: During the 1980s, an Okanagan Lake tourism association offered a one-million-dollar reward for anyone who could provide “living proof” that Ogopogo really existed.

claims.statement: In 1991 a scientific expedition made a high-tech search of the lake for evidence of a giant aquatic creature, using an underwater remote-controlled vehicle and a submarine, but no sign of an Ogopogo was discovered.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1991, sebuah ekspedisi ilmiah mencari bukti di danau dengan teknologi tinggi bahwa danau itu rumah bagi makhluk air raksasa. Ekspedisi itu memakai kendaraan bawah air kendali jarak jauh dan kapal selam, tetapi tak ada tanda Ogopogo ditemukan.
claims.quote: In 1991, a scientific expedition conducted a high-tech search of the lake for evidence that it was home to a giant aquatic creature. The expedition included an underwater remote-controlled vehicle and a submarine, but no sign of an Ogopogo was discovered.

claims.statement: A more logical explanation is that the "monster" may be a large fish such as a sturgeon, and an even more plausible one is that Ogopogo may be nothing more than a phenomenon caused by the lake's geology.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan yang lebih logis adalah bahwa "monster" itu mungkin ikan besar seperti sturgeon. Penjelasan yang lebih masuk akal lagi adalah bahwa Ogopogo mungkin hanyalah fenomena akibat geologi danau.
claims.quote: A more logical explanation is that the “monster” may be a large fish such as a sturgeon. ... An even more plausible explanation is that Ogopogo may be nothing more than a phenomenon caused by the lake’s geology.

claims.statement: The creature was most often said to be multi-humped with the head of a horse and green, black, or gray skin; other reports claimed the head of a goat, a snake, or even an alligator.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu paling sering dikatakan berpunuk banyak dengan kepala kuda dan kulit hijau, hitam, atau abu-abu. Laporan lain menyebut kepalanya seperti kambing, ular, atau bahkan aligator.
claims.quote: The creature was most often said to be multi-humped with the head of a horse and green, black, or gray skin. Other reports claimed that it had the head of a goat, a snake, or even an alligator.

claims.statement: The creature may sometimes be referred to by the pet name Oggy, and smaller creatures may be referred to as Ogopups.
claims.statement_id: Selain itu, makhluk ini kadang disebut dengan nama sayang Oggy. Makhluk yang lebih kecil dapat disebut Ogopup.
claims.quote: Additionally, the creature may sometimes be referred to by the pet name Oggy. Smaller creatures may be referred to as Ogopups.

claims.statement: Stories of the lake monster were featured on American television shows such as Unsolved Mysteries and In Search Of.
claims.statement_id: Kisah monster danau itu diangkat dalam acara televisi Amerika seperti Unsolved Mysteries dan In Search Of.
claims.quote: Stories of the lake monster were featured on American television shows such as Unsolved Mysteries and In Search Of.

claims.statement: The Ogopogo now plays a role in the commercial symbolism and media representation of the region.
claims.statement_id: Ogopogo kini berperan dalam simbol komersial dan representasi media kawasan itu.
claims.quote: The Ogopogo now plays a role in the commercial symbolism and media representation of the region.

claims.statement: Like Scotland's famed Loch Ness monster, Ogopogo has become a local tourist attraction and even inspired a one-million-dollar bounty for proof of its existence.
claims.statement_id: Seperti monster Loch Ness yang terkenal di Skotlandia, Ogopogo menjadi atraksi wisata setempat dan bahkan memicu hadiah satu juta dolar bagi bukti keberadaannya.
claims.quote: Similar to Scotland’s famed Loch Ness monster, Ogopogo has become a local tourist attraction and even inspired a one-million-dollar bounty for proof of its existence.

claims.statement: The word "n'ha-a-itk" has various translations, such as "water-demon", "water god", or "sacred creature of the water".
claims.statement_id: Kata "n'ha-a-itk" punya beberapa terjemahan, seperti "iblis air", "dewa air", atau "makhluk suci air".
claims.quote: The word "n'ha-a-itk" has various translations, such as "water-demon", "water god", or "sacred creature of the water".

claims.statement: As outsiders began to move into the region in the nineteenth century they heard stories of N'ha-a-itk and interpreted the spirit as a giant snake-like monster.
claims.statement_id: Ketika orang luar mulai pindah ke kawasan itu pada abad ke-19, mereka mendengar kisah tentang N'ha-a-itk dan menafsirkan roh itu sebagai monster raksasa menyerupai ular.
claims.quote: As outsiders began to move into the region in the nineteenth century, they heard stories of N’ha-a-itk and interpreted the spirit as a giant snake-like monster.

claims.statement: The spirit was said to dwell in caves under Rattlesnake Island (a.k.a. Monster Island) or adjacent to Squally Point.
claims.statement_id: Roh itu dikatakan berdiam di gua-gua di bawah Rattlesnake Island (alias Monster Island) atau di dekat Squally Point.
claims.quote: The spirit was said to dwell in caves under Rattlesnake Island (a.k.a. Monster Island) or adjacent to Squally Point.

claims.statement: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, Sanna; previously Sedna or Sidne) is the goddess of the sea and marine animals in Inuit religion, also known as the Mother of the Sea or Mistress of the Sea.
claims.statement_id: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, Sanna; sebelumnya Sedna atau Sidne) adalah dewi laut dan hewan laut dalam agama Inuit, juga dikenal sebagai Ibu Laut atau Nyonya Laut.
claims.quote: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, romanized: Sanna , previously Sedna or Sidne) is the goddess of the sea and marine animals in Inuit religion, also known as the Mother of the Sea or Mistress of the Sea.

claims.statement: The story of Sedna, a creation myth, describes how she came to rule over Adlivun, the Inuit equivalent of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Sedna, yang merupakan mitos penciptaan, menceritakan bagaimana ia sampai menguasai Adlivun, padanan dunia bawah dalam kepercayaan Inuit.
claims.quote: The story of Sedna, which is a creation myth, describes how she came to rule over Adlivun, the Inuit equivalent of the underworld.

claims.statement: Most of her names are avoidance-speech workarounds, owing to a custom of avoiding the proper name of one who is feared or deserves respect; Sanna means "the great one down below" and Sedna is an older spelling.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar namanya adalah penghindaran penyebutan nama asli, karena kebiasaan menghindari nama sebenarnya dari sosok yang ditakuti atau patut dihormati. Sanna berarti "yang agung di bawah sana", dan Sedna adalah ejaan yang lebih tua.
claims.quote: Most of her names are avoidance speech workarounds, due to a custom of avoiding the proper name of one fearful or deserving of respect. ... Sanna (ᓴᓐᓇ ) meaning "the great one down below". Sedna is an older spelling.

claims.statement: An origin myth tells how Sedna was once a girl thrown overboard from a vessel; her fingers were cut off at the joints as she held on, the segments turned into sea mammals, and she sank to the sea bottom and became the Sea Woman, who controlled these animals.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah mitos asal-usul menceritakan bahwa Sedna dulunya seorang gadis yang dilempar dari kapal. Saat ia berpegangan, jari-jarinya dipotong di ruas-ruasnya. Ia tenggelam ke dasar laut, ruas-ruas jarinya menjadi mamalia laut, dan ia menjadi Wanita Laut (Sea Woman) yang menguasai hewan-hewan itu.
claims.quote: An origin myth tells how Sedna was once a girl who was thrown overboard from a vessel. While she tried to hang on, her fingers were cut off at the joints. She sank to the bottom of the sea, the segments of her fingers turning into sea mammals, and she became the Sea Woman, who was in control of these animals.

claims.statement: Franz Boas, in his 1888 monograph on the Inuit of Baffin Island, gave her name as Sedna, which probably means "the one down there"; other Inuit groups used other names for the Sea Woman, such as Nerrivik (Polar Inuit, "the place of the food") and Nuliajuk (Netsilik Inuit, "the lubricious one").
claims.statement_id: Franz Boas, dalam monografnya tentang orang Inuit di Pulau Baffin (1888), menuliskan namanya sebagai Sedna, yang kemungkinan berarti "yang di bawah sana". Kelompok Inuit lain menyebut Wanita Laut dengan nama berbeda, misalnya Nerrivik (Inuit Kutub, "tempat makanan") dan Nuliajuk (Inuit Netsilik, "si birahi").
claims.quote: Franz Boas, in his monograph about the Inuit on Baffin Island (1888), gave her name as Sedna, which probably means "the one down there." Other Inuit groups referred to the Sea Woman under different names, such as Nerrivik (Polar Inuit, "the place of the food") and Nuliajuk (Netsilik Inuit, "the lubricious one").

claims.statement: She became the Sea Woman, who controlled these animals, and according to some Iglulik Inuit and Baffin Islanders she also ruled over the souls of those who had gone to the undersea land of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi Wanita Laut yang menguasai hewan-hewan itu. Menurut sebagian orang Iglulik Inuit dan penduduk Baffin, ia juga menguasai jiwa orang-orang yang telah pergi ke negeri orang mati di bawah laut.
claims.quote: she became the Sea Woman, who was in control of these animals. According to some Iglulik Inuit and Baffin Islanders, she also ruled over the souls of those who had gone to the undersea land of the dead.

claims.statement: In some variants the girl's father forces her to marry a dog because she refused to marry; her children become Indians, white people, and so on, so the mother of the sea animals is made the mother of men as well and represents the female principle of the world.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian varian, ayah sang gadis memaksanya menikah dengan anjing karena ia menolak menikah. Anak-anaknya menjadi orang Indian, orang kulit putih, dan seterusnya. Dengan demikian ibu hewan laut juga dijadikan ibu manusia dan melambangkan prinsip feminin dunia.
claims.quote: In some variants the girl's father forces her to marry a dog because she has refused to marry. Her children become Indians, white people, and so on. In this way the mother of the sea animals is made the mother of men as well; as such, she represents the female principle of the world.

claims.statement: According to Inuit belief the Sea Woman could withhold the sea animals when certain hunting, birth, and death taboos were broken; in Greenland the transgressions were said to become dirt in her hair, making her uncomfortable, and having no fingers she could not comb it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Inuit, Wanita Laut berkuasa menahan hewan laut bila pantangan tertentu tentang perburuan, kelahiran, dan kematian dilanggar. Di Greenland diceritakan bahwa pelanggaran itu menjadi kotoran di rambutnya hingga ia tidak nyaman; karena tak berjari, ia tidak dapat menyisir rambutnya.
claims.quote: According to Inuit belief, the Sea Woman had the power to withhold the sea animals when certain hunting, birth, and death taboos had been broken. In Greenland it was told that the transgressions would materialize as dirt in the Sea Woman's hair, making her feel uncomfortable; because she had no fingers, she was unable to comb her hair.

claims.statement: Before the shaman could comb Sedna's hair he had to fight her; afterward she would set the sea animals free and the shaman would return.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum dapat menyisir rambut Sedna, sang dukun harus melawannya. Setelah itu ia membebaskan hewan-hewan laut, dan sang dukun kembali.
claims.quote: Before the shaman could comb Sedna's hair he had to fight her. Afterward, she would set the sea animals free, and the shaman would return

claims.statement: The Inuit on Baffin Island held great multi-day feasts in which Sedna was ritually killed; these calendar feasts took place in autumn, when storms breaking the ice prevented sealing.
claims.statement_id: Orang Inuit di Pulau Baffin menggelar pesta besar berhari-hari yang di dalamnya Sedna dibunuh secara ritual. Pesta kalender ini berlangsung pada musim gugur ketika badai memecahkan es sehingga perburuan anjing laut terhalang.
claims.quote: The Inuit on Baffin Island held great feasts, lasting several days, in which Sedna was ritually killed. These calendar feasts took place in the autumn when sealing was prevented by storms that broke the ice open.

claims.statement: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of nearly all Inuit existence, so the relationship with the Sea Woman was important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.
claims.statement_id: Anjing laut dan hewan laut lain menjadi dasar kehidupan hampir semua orang Inuit. Karena itu hubungan dengan Wanita Laut penting tetapi sangat peka: ia tidak hanya menguasai hewan-hewan itu, mereka berasal darinya.
claims.quote: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of the existence of nearly all Inuit. The relationship with the Sea Woman was therefore important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.

claims.statement: Variants of the myth have been recorded from many localities in Greenland and Canada but from Alaska only one reference exists; in some an orphan girl is thrown overboard, but more often a girl is fooled into marrying a petrel that had taken human form.
claims.statement_id: Varian mitos ini tercatat dari banyak tempat di Greenland dan Kanada, tetapi dari Alaska hanya ada satu rujukan. Dalam sebagian varian seorang gadis yatim dilempar dari kapal, tetapi lebih sering mitos dimulai dengan gadis yang ditipu menikahi seekor petrel yang berwujud manusia.
claims.quote: Variants of this myth have been recorded from many localities in Greenland and Canada, but from Alaska only a single reference exists. In some variants an orphan girl is thrown overboard, but more often the myth begins with the story of a girl who was fooled into marrying a petrel that had taken on human form.

claims.statement: The father tried to pacify the petrel by throwing his daughter overboard; when she clung to the boat he cut off her fingers at the first joint, and the fingertips became small seals, and at the next joint the segments became big, bearded seals.
claims.statement_id: Sang ayah berusaha menenangkan petrel dengan melempar putrinya ke laut. Ketika ia berpegangan pada sisi perahu, ayahnya memotong jarinya pada ruas pertama; ujung jarinya jatuh ke laut dan menjadi anjing laut kecil. Ketika ia kembali berpegangan, ayahnya memotong pada ruas berikutnya; potongan itu menjadi anjing laut besar berjanggut.
claims.quote: The father tried to pacify the petrel by throwing his daughter overboard. When she tried to cling to the side of the boat, her father cut off her fingers at the first joint. Her fingertips fell into the sea and became small seals. When she again grasped the side of the boat, her father cut off her fingers at the next joint; these segments fell into the sea and became big, bearded seals.

claims.statement: When she still clung with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint and these segments turned into walruses; sometimes the order differs, with whales created first (the girl's nails are linked to baleen), then small seals and bearded seals.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ia masih berpegangan dengan sisa-sisa jarinya, ayahnya memotongnya pada ruas terakhir dan potongan itu menjadi walrus. Kadang urutan terciptanya hewan laut berbeda: paus tercipta lebih dulu (kuku sang gadis dikaitkan dengan balin), disusul anjing laut kecil dan anjing laut berjanggut.
claims.quote: When she still clung to the side of the boat with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint, and these segments turned into walruses. Sometimes the order of the creation of the sea animals is different, with whales being created first (the girl's nails are associated with baleen), followed by small seals and bearded seals.

claims.statement: Traditional Inuit tattoos often include lines across a woman's fingers, knuckles, or wrists, alluding to the story of where Sedna's fingers were cut, and some say Sedna denies access to the afterlife to women whose fingers were not tattooed.
claims.statement_id: Tato tradisional Inuit sering memuat garis melintang di jari, buku jari, atau pergelangan tangan perempuan, merujuk pada kisah tempat jari Sedna dipotong. Sebagian orang mengatakan Sedna menolak jalan ke alam baka bagi perempuan yang jarinya tidak bertato.
claims.quote: Traditional Inuit tattoos often include lines across a woman's fingers, knuckles, or wrists, alluding to the story of where Sedna's fingers were cut. Some say Sedna denies access to the afterlife to women whose fingers weren’t tattooed.

claims.statement: In art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni, Sedna biasanya digambarkan berkepala dan berbadan atas perempuan dengan ekor mamalia laut, mirip putri duyung.
claims.quote: in art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.

claims.statement: The trans-Neptunian object 90377 Sedna, discovered on November 14, 2003, is named after her.
claims.statement_id: Objek trans-Neptunus 90377 Sedna, yang ditemukan pada 14 November 2003, dinamai menurut namanya.
claims.quote: 90377 Sedna, a trans-Neptunian object discovered by ... on November 14, 2003, is named after her.

claims.statement: In East Asian mythology the rabbit is seen pounding with a mortar and pestle, but the contents of the mortar differ among Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese folklore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Asia Timur, kelinci dilihat sedang menumbuk dengan lesung dan alu, tetapi isi lesung berbeda-beda dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok, Jepang, Korea, dan Vietnam.
claims.quote: In East Asian mythology, the rabbit is seen as pounding with a mortar and pestle, but the contents of the mortar differ among Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese folklore.

claims.statement: In some Chinese versions the rabbit pounds medicine for mortals, and some include the making of mooncakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi Tiongkok, kelinci menumbuk obat bagi manusia fana dan sebagian memuat pembuatan kue bulan.
claims.quote: In some Chinese versions, the rabbit pounds medicine for the mortals and some include making of mooncakes.

claims.statement: Knowing only how to gather grass, the rabbit offered its own body by throwing itself into a fire the man had prepared; the rabbit was not burnt and the old man revealed himself as Śakra, who, touched by its virtue, drew the likeness of the rabbit on the Moon for all to see.
claims.statement_id: Karena hanya tahu mengumpulkan rumput, kelinci menawarkan tubuhnya sendiri dengan melompat ke api yang disiapkan lelaki tua itu. Namun kelinci tidak terbakar dan lelaki tua itu mengungkapkan dirinya Śakra. Tersentuh oleh kebajikan sang kelinci, ia menggambar rupa kelinci itu di Bulan agar semua orang melihatnya.
claims.quote: Knowing only how to gather grass, the rabbit instead offered its own body by throwing itself into a fire the man had prepared. However, the rabbit was not burnt and the old man revealed that he was Śakra. Touched by the rabbit's virtue, he drew the likeness of the rabbit on the Moon for all to see.

claims.statement: Moon folklore from certain Amerindian cultures of North America also has rabbit themes and characters.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat tentang bulan dari beberapa budaya Amerindian di Amerika Utara juga memuat tema dan tokoh kelinci.
claims.quote: Moon folklore from certain Amerindian cultures of North America also has rabbit themes and characters.

claims.statement: The Moon rabbit, Moon hare or Jade rabbit is a mythical figure in both East Asian and indigenous American folklore, based on interpretations that identify the dark markings on the near side of the Moon as a rabbit or hare.
claims.statement_id: Kelinci bulan, hare bulan, atau kelinci giok adalah tokoh mitos dalam cerita rakyat Asia Timur dan pribumi Amerika, berdasarkan tafsiran yang mengenali bercak gelap di sisi dekat Bulan sebagai kelinci atau hare.
claims.quote: The Moon rabbit, Moon hare or Jade rabbit is a mythical figure in both East Asian and indigenous American folklore, based on interpretations that identify the dark markings on the near side of the Moon as a rabbit or hare.

claims.statement: An early Chinese source, the Chu Ci, a Western Han anthology of poems from the Warring States period, notes that along with a toad there is a hare on the Moon who constantly pounds herbs for the immortals.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Tiongkok awal bernama Chu Ci, antologi puisi Han Barat dari zaman Negara-Negara Berperang, mencatat bahwa di samping seekor kodok, ada seekor hare di Bulan yang terus menumbuk ramuan bagi para makhluk abadi.
claims.quote: An early Chinese source called the Chu Ci, a Western Han anthology of Chinese poems from the Warring States period, notes that along with a toad, there is a hare on the Moon who constantly pounds herbs for the immortals.

claims.statement: Han dynasty poets call the hare on the Moon the "Jade Hare" (玉兔) or the "Gold Hare" (金兔), and these phrases were often used in place of the word for the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Para penyair dinasti Han menyebut hare di Bulan "Hare Giok" (玉兔) atau "Hare Emas" (金兔), dan ungkapan itu sering dipakai menggantikan kata untuk Bulan.
claims.quote: Han dynasty poets call the hare on the Moon the "Jade Hare" (玉兔 ) or the "Gold Hare" (金兔 ), and these phrases were used often, in place of the word for the Moon.

claims.statement: In Chinese folklore the rabbit Yutu is often portrayed as a companion of the Moon goddess Chang'e, constantly pounding the elixir of life for her, and some versions show the making of cakes or rice cakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok, kelinci bernama Yutu sering digambarkan sebagai pendamping dewi Bulan Chang'e, yang terus menumbuk eliksir kehidupan untuknya; sebagian menampilkan pembuatan kue atau kue beras.
claims.quote: In Chinese folklore, the rabbit, Yutu, is often portrayed as a companion of the Moon goddess Chang'e, constantly pounding the elixir of life for her and some show the making of cakes or rice cakes

claims.statement: In the Buddhist Jataka tales, Tale 316 relates that a monkey, an otter, a jackal, and a rabbit resolved to practice charity on the full-moon day (Uposatha), believing great virtue would earn a great reward.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Jataka Buddhis, Kisah 316 menceritakan seekor monyet, berang-berang, jakal, dan kelinci bertekad berderma pada hari bulan purnama (Uposatha), percaya bahwa menunjukkan kebajikan besar akan mendatangkan ganjaran besar.
claims.quote: In the Buddhist Jataka tales, Tale 316 relates that a monkey, an otter, a jackal, and a rabbit resolved to practice charity on the day of the full moon (Uposatha), believing a demonstration of great virtue would earn a great reward.

claims.statement: This legend also gave rise to the Mid-Autumn Festivals of China, Tết Trung Thu of Vietnam, Tsukimi of Japan, Chuseok of Korea, and Bon Om Touk in Cambodia, all of which celebrate the legend of the Moon rabbit.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini juga melahirkan Festival Pertengahan Musim Gugur di Tiongkok, Tết Trung Thu di Vietnam, Tsukimi di Jepang, Chuseok di Korea, dan Bon Om Touk di Kamboja, yang semuanya merayakan legenda kelinci bulan.
claims.quote: This legend also gave rise to the Mid-Autumn Festivals of China, Tết Trung Thu of Vietnam, Tsukimi of Japan, and Chuseok of Korea, and Bon Om Touk in Cambodia, all of which celebrate the legend of the Moon rabbit.

claims.statement: According to an Aztec legend, Quetzalcoatl, living on Earth as a human, started a journey; a rabbit grazing nearby offered herself as food to save his life, and moved by the offering he elevated her to the Moon before returning her to Earth, imprinting her image in the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Aztec, dewa Quetzalcoatl yang saat itu hidup di Bumi sebagai manusia memulai sebuah perjalanan ... seekor kelinci yang merumput di dekatnya menawarkan dirinya sebagai makanan untuk menyelamatkan nyawanya. Tergerak oleh persembahan mulia itu, Quetzalcoatl mengangkat sang kelinci ke Bulan sebelum mengembalikannya ke Bumi, dan menorehkan rupanya di Bulan.
claims.quote: According to an Aztec legend, the god Quetzalcoatl, then living on Earth as a human, started on a journey ... a rabbit grazing nearby offered herself as food to save his life. Quetzalcoatl, moved by the rabbit's noble offering, elevated her to the Moon before returning her to Earth, imprinting her image in the Moon.

claims.statement: In a Cree cultural legend a young rabbit wished to ride the Moon, but only the crane was willing to take him there, and the trip stretched the crane's legs, leaving them elongated.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda budaya Cree, seekor kelinci muda ingin menunggang Bulan, tetapi hanya burung bangau yang bersedia membawanya ke sana. Perjalanan itu meregangkan kaki sang bangau hingga memanjang.
claims.quote: In a Cree cultural legend, a young rabbit wished to ride the Moon, but only the crane was willing to take him there. The trip stretched the crane's legs, leaving them elongated.

claims.statement: Because of Tecciztecatl's cowardice, the other deities believed the Moon should not be as bright as the Sun and threw a rabbit at Tecciztecatl's face to diminish his light.
claims.statement_id: Karena kepengecutan Tecciztecatl, para dewa lain menganggap Bulan tidak boleh seterang Matahari dan melemparkan seekor kelinci ke wajah Tecciztecatl untuk meredupkan cahayanya.
claims.quote: Due to Tecciztecatl's cowardice, the other deities believed that the Moon should not be as bright as the Sun and threw a rabbit at Tecciztecatl's face to diminish his light.

claims.statement: In Asia a white hare is said to inhabit the moon; an early version of the story of how the hare came to live there is in the Jataka Tales from India about the Buddha's incarnations before he was born as Gautama Buddha (tale 316).
claims.statement_id: Di Asia, seekor hare putih dikatakan mendiami bulan. Versi awal kisah bagaimana hare itu tinggal di bulan terdapat dalam Kisah Jataka dari India tentang inkarnasi Buddha sebelum lahir sebagai Gautama Buddha (kisah 316).
claims.quote: In Asia, a white hare is said to inhabit the moon. An early version of the story of how the hare came to live on the moon can be found in the Jataka Tales from India concerning the incarnations of the Buddha before being born as Gautama Buddha (tale 316).

claims.statement: The man reveals that he is the deity Sakra and prevents the hare from being burned, then takes him to live on the moon for eternity so that his selflessness can be witnessed by the world.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki itu mengungkapkan dirinya dewa Sakra dan mencegah hare itu terbakar. Lalu ia membawanya tinggal di bulan untuk selamanya agar ketidakegoisannya disaksikan dunia.
